question: Nígbà wo ni ìforúkọsílẹ̀ àwọn olóyè gbọ́dọ̀ dẹ́kun ṣáájú ìdìbò?
answer: Ìgbìmọ̀ gbọ́dọ̀ dẹ́kun ìforúkọsílẹ̀ àwọn olóyè ní ọgọ́rùn-ún (90) ọjọ́ ṣáájú ìdìbò. Ìbéèrè yìí wà nínú Ìwé-òfin Ìdìbò, 2026, Ìpín 9(6) [act-s9-0].
src_question: When must voter registration stop before an election?
src_answer: The Commission must stop registration at least 90 days before any election. This requirement is stated in Section 9(6) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s9-0].

question: Ní àwọn ìdásí wo ni Ìforúkọsílẹ̀ Àwọn Olóyè Orílẹ̀-èdè gbọ́dọ̀ wà?
answer: Ìgbìmọ̀ gbọ́dọ̀ fi Ìforúkọsílẹ̀ Àwọn Olóyè Orílẹ̀-èdè sílẹ̀ nínú ìdásí ẹlẹ́kùtírónìkì nínú ìdátà àgbà wọn àti nínú ìdásí àtẹ̀wé, tí a tẹ̀ jáde lórí ìwé. Ìbéèrè yìí wà nínú Ìwé-òfin Ìdìbò, 2026, Ìpín 9(2) [act-s9-0].
src_question: In what formats must the National Register of Voters be kept?
src_answer: The Commission must keep the Register of Voters in electronic format in its central database and in manual, printed, paper-based format. This is required by Section 9(2) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s9-0].

question: Kí ni àwọn ìwé tí ènìyàn lè fi hàn láti forúkọsílẹ̀ gẹ́gẹ́ bí olóyè nínú ìforúkọsílẹ̀ títọ́?
answer: Fún ìforúkọsílẹ̀ títọ́, ènìyàn gbọ́dọ̀ wá síbẹ̀ pẹ̀lú ìwé ìbí orílẹ̀-èdè, ìwé ìrìn-àjò orílẹ̀-èdè, tàbí Nọ́mbà Ìdánimọ̀ Orílẹ̀-èdè (NIN). Ìbéèrè yìí wà nínú Ìwé-òfin Ìdìbò, 2026, Ìpín 10(2) [act-s10-0].
src_question: What documents can a person present to register as a voter under continuous registration?
src_answer: For continuous registration, a person must appear in person with a Nigerian birth certificate, a Nigerian passport, or a National Identification Number (NIN). This requirement is in Section 10(2) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s10-0].

question: Nígbà tí ìdìbò gbogbogbò bá tiẹ̀ jáde, èyí ni ìwé ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ àwọn olùdìbò tí a fi lò fún ìdìbò yẹn?
answer: Ìwé ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ àwọn olùdìbò tí a fi lò fún ìdìbò gbogbogbò ni Ìwé Ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ Àwọn Olùdìbò tí a ṣàkíyèsí láti ọwọ́ Kọ́míṣọ̀nù. Ẹ̀ka 10(4) ti Ìwé Ìdìbò, 2026 ń fún ìdílé yìí [act-s10-0].
src_question: When a general election is announced, which voters' register is used for that election?
src_answer: The official voters' register for a general election is the current Register of Voters certified by the Commission. Section 10(4) of the Electoral Act, 2026 requires this [act-s10-0].

question: Ṣé àwọn olùkọ́kọ́ ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ lè jẹ́ ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ àwọn ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú?
answer: Àwọn olùkọ́kọ́ tí a yàn fún ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ àwọn olùdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ má jẹ́ ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú kankan. Ìdílé yìí wà nínú Ẹ̀ka 11(1) ti Ìwé Ìdìbò, 2026 [act-s11-0].
src_question: Can registration officers be members of political parties?
src_answer: Officers appointed for voter registration must not belong to any political party. This is mandated by Section 11(1) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s11-0].

question: Kí ni ó máa ṣẹlẹ̀ bí olùdìbò bá kò sọ̀rọ̀ sí olùkọ́kọ́ ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ nígbà ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀?
answer: Àìsọ̀rọ̀ olùdìbò sí olùkọ́kọ́ ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ kò máa ṣe ìwé ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ di aláìlẹ́ṣẹ́. Ẹ̀ka 11(2) ti Ìwé Ìdìbò, 2026 ń sọ ìdílé yìí [act-s11-0].
src_question: What happens if a voter does not object to a registration officer during the registration process?
src_answer: A voter’s failure to object to a registration officer does not make the register invalid. Section 11(2) of the Electoral Act, 2026 states this rule [act-s11-0].

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ fún ìforúkọsílẹ̀ lọ́pọ̀lọpọ̀ níbi kan náà?
answer: Ẹni tó bá forúkọsílẹ̀ lọ́pọ̀lọpọ̀ níbi kan náà lè ní ìdájọ́ tí ó tó N100,000, tàbí ìgbàlódé ọdún kan, tàbí gbogbo wọn. Ìdájọ́ yìí wà nínú Ìwé-òfin Ìdìbò, 2026, Ìwé 12(3) [act-s12-0].
src_question: What is the penalty for registering more than once in the same registration centre?
src_answer: A person who registers more than once in the same centre may be fined at least N100,000, imprisoned for at least one year, or receive both penalties. This penalty is set out in Section 12(3) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s12-0].

question: Mo lọ sí ìjọba ìbílẹ̀ mìíràn ṣáájú ìdìbò. Ṣé mo lè tún ṣe ìdìbò níbẹ̀?
answer: Bẹ́ẹ̀ ni, o lè wá láti wá sí Àkójọ Àwọn Tí Wọ́n Tún Ṣe Ìdìbò Tí Wọ́n Jẹ́ Olùgbé Ní Ìjọba Ìbílẹ̀ Tuntun bí o bá jẹ́ olùgbé ní àgbègbè ìdìbò tuntun àti pé o ti wà ní ìwé ìdìbò níbẹ̀. O gbọ́dọ̀ fúnni ní àkọ́kọ́ ìwé ìdìbò rẹ àti ṣe ìbéèrè náà kí ó tó 90 ọjọ́ ṣáájú ọjọ́ ìdìbò ní ìjọba ìbílẹ̀ náà. Olùṣàkóso Ìdìbò Olùgbé yóò pinnu bóyá láti fi orúkọ rẹ sí àkójọ náà. [act-s13-0]
src_question: I moved to a different constituency before the election. Can I still vote there?
src_answer: Yes, you can apply to be entered on the Transferred Voters List if you are resident in a polling area of the new constituency and are registered elsewhere. You must submit a copy of your voters' card and make the application not later than 90 days before the date of an election in that constituency. The Resident Electoral Commissioner will decide whether to add your name to the list. [act-s13-0]

question: Kí ni iṣẹ́ olùṣàkóso ìdìbò lẹ́yìn tí orúkọ mi ti wà lórí Àtòjọ Àwọn Olùdìbò Tí A Gbé Kalẹ̀?
answer: Lẹ́yìn tí orúkọ rẹ ti wà lórí Àtòjọ Àwọn Olùdìbò Tí A Gbé Kalẹ̀, olùṣàkóso ìdìbò yóò fi ọ́ sí ipò ìdìbò tàbí àgbègbè ìdìbò nínú ìjọba àgbègbè, ó sì máa fi ìfihàn náà sí àtòjọ. Olùṣàkóso náà yóò sì fún ọ ní káríìdè olùdìbò tuntun, ó sì máa gba káríìdè tẹ́lẹ̀ rẹ. Àkọ́kọ́ ìfihàn náà yóò sì rán sí olùṣàkóso ìdìbò nínú ìjọba àgbègbè. [act-s13-0]
src_question: What does the electoral officer do after my name is added to the Transferred Voters List?
src_answer: After your name is entered on the Transferred Voters List, an electoral officer assigns you to a polling station or polling area in the constituency and indicates the assignment in the list. The officer then issues you a new voters' card and retrieves your previous card. A copy of the entry is sent to the electoral officer of the constituency. [act-s13-0]

question: Bí mo bá kò lè kà tàbí kọ, ṣé ẹnikẹ́ni lè kún fọ́ọ̀mù ìforúkọsílẹ̀ fún mi?
answer: Bẹ́ẹ̀ ni, bí o bá jẹ́ aláìlẹ́kọ̀ọ́ tàbí aláìsàn, olùṣàkóso ìforúkọsílẹ̀ lè kún fọ́ọ̀mù náà lórí ìbéèrè rẹ. Èyí yóò ràn ọ́ lọ́wọ́ láti ṣe ìbéèrè ìforúkọsílẹ̀ láìsí láti kà tàbí kọ. [act-s14-0]
src_question: If I cannot read or write, can someone else fill out my registration form?
src_answer: Yes, if you are illiterate or disabled, the registration officer may complete the application form on your request. This helps you meet the registration requirement without needing to read or write. [act-s14-0]

question: Báwo ni mo ṣe lè rí àkọ́kọ́ ìwé ìfọwọ́sí ti àtòjọ àwọn olùdìbò fún ìpínlẹ̀ mi?
answer: O lè rí àkọ́kọ́ ìwé ìfọwọ́sí ti àtòjọ àwọn olùdìbò fún ìpínlẹ̀ rẹ nípa ìfọwọ́sí sí Kọ́míṣọ̀nà. Àkọ́kọ́ náà lè jẹ́ fún ìpínlẹ̀ gbogbo, ìjọba àgbègbè, àgbègbè ìjọba, tàbí àwọn ipò ìdìbò tàbí àgbègbè ìforúkọsílẹ̀ kan. [act-s15-0]
src_question: How can I obtain a certified copy of the voters' register for my state?
src_answer: You can obtain a certified true copy of the voters' register for your state by applying to the Commission. The copy may be for the whole State, a Local Government, an Area Council, or specific polling units or registration areas. [act-s15-0]

question: Ṣé mo gbọ́dọ̀ san owó láti gba àkọ́kọ́ ìwé ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ àwọn èèyàn tí wọ́n ń ṣe ìdìbò?
answer: Bẹ́ẹ̀ni, o gbọ́dọ̀ san owó tí Ìjọba Ìdìbò (INEC) ṣètò láti gba àkọ́kọ́ ìwé ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ àwọn èèyàn tí wọ́n ń ṣe ìdìbò. Owó náà ni Ìjọba Ìdìbò ṣètò, ó sì gbọ́dọ̀ wà níbẹ̀ kí wọ́n tó lè fún ọ ní àkọ́kọ́ náà. [act-s15-0]
src_question: Do I have to pay to get a copy of the voters' register?
src_answer: Yes, you must pay the fees that the Commission determines to obtain a certified copy of the voters' register. The fees are set by the Commission and are required before the copy is issued. [act-s15-0]

question: Ṣé ó gba láti ní ìwé ìdánilójú olùdìbò méjì?
answer: Rárá, olùdìbò kò gbọ́dọ̀ ní ìwé ìdánilójú olùdìbò méjì. Gbígbé ìwé ìdánilójú méjì jẹ́ ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ ìsọ̀rọ̀ (2) ti Òfin. [act-s16-0]
src_question: Is it allowed to have more than one voters' card?
src_answer: No, a voter shall not hold more than one valid voters' card. Holding more than one card violates subsection (2) of the Act. [act-s16-0]

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ tí mo máa rí bí mo bá ní àwọn káríayé olóyè tó pọ̀ ju ọ̀kan lọ?
answer: Bí o bá ní àwọn káríayé olóyè tó pọ̀ ju ọ̀kan lọ, o ti ṣe ẹ̀ṣẹ̀, o sì lè rí owó ìdájọ́ tó tó N500,000, tàbí kí o wà ní ìdájọ́ fún ọdún kan, tàbí méjèèjì. Ìdájọ́ yìí máa ń wáyé lẹ́yìn tí ilé-ẹjọ́ bá ti fi ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ rẹ̀ múlẹ̀. [act-s16-0]
src_question: What penalty do I face if I hold more than one voters' card?
src_answer: If you hold more than one valid voters' card, you commit an offence and may be fined up to N500,000, imprisoned for up to one year, or both. The penalty applies upon conviction by a court. [act-s16-0]

question: Kí ni gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe bí mo bá pa àwòrán ìdájọ́ mi ṣẹ́ ṣáájú ìdìbò?
answer: Bí àwòrán ìdájọ́ bá pa, pa dà, yí padà, tàbí ṣe àìsàn míì, olùdájọ́ gbọ́dọ̀ wá sí ọ̀gá ìdìbò tàbí ẹnikẹ́ni tí a fún ní ìyàtọ̀ láti wá sí i, kò gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ 90 ọjọ́ ṣáájú ọjọ́ ìdìbò, kí ó sọ àwọn ìdí . Olùdájọ́ lè tún ṣe àwòrán ìdájọ́ tuntun. [act-s18-0]
src_question: What must I do if I lose my voter's card before the election?
src_answer: If a voter's card is lost, destroyed, defaced, torn or otherwise damaged, the owner must apply in person to the electoral officer or any authorised officer not less than 90 days before polling day, stating the circumstances [act-s18-0]. The owner may also print a downloadable copy.

question: Ṣé mo lè gba àwòrán ìdájọ́ tuntun kéré ju 90 ọjọ́ ṣáájú ọjọ́ ìdìbò, àti kí ni ìdájọ́ tí a ó fi sí ẹni tí ó bá ṣe àìsàn yìí?
answer: Àwòrán ìdájọ́ tuntun kò gbọ́dọ̀ wá sí ẹni kéré ju 90 ọjọ́ ṣáájú ọjọ́ ìdìbò. Ẹnikẹ́ni tí ó bá ṣe àìsàn yìí ń ṣe ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀. Ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ yìí ń fi ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ N200,000, ìdájọ́ títí di ọdún méjì, tàbí méjèèjì, gẹ́gẹ́ bí a ti sọ nínú Òfin . [act-s18-0]
src_question: Can I receive a replacement voter's card less than 90 days before polling day, and what are the penalties if someone issues it?
src_answer: A replacement permanent voter's card may not be issued to any voter less than 90 days before polling day. Anyone who issues a replacement in violation of this rule commits an offence. The offence carries a fine of up to N200,000, imprisonment for up to two years, or both, as set out in the Act [act-s18-0].

question: Nígbà wo ni Ẹ̀ka Ìdìbò Yóò fi Àkójọ Àwọn Olùdájọ́ hàn fún Ìwádìí Gbangba?
answer: Ẹ̀ka Ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ fi Àkójọ Àwọn Olùdájọ́ hàn fún Ìwádìí Gbangba kò gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ 90 ọjọ́ ṣáájú ìdìbò gbogbogbò. Àkókò ìwádìí ń jẹ́ ọjọ́ méje, àti pé àkójọ náà ń hàn ní gbogbo ibi ìdájọ́ àti lórí ojú ìkànnì Ẹ̀ka Ìdìbò [act-s19-0].
src_question: When will the Commission display the voters' register for public scrutiny?
src_answer: The Commission must display the voters' register for public scrutiny not later than 90 days before a general election. The display period lasts seven days and the register is shown at each registration area and on the Commission's website [act-s19-0].

question: Báwo ni àkókò tí mo ní láti gbé ìdájọ́ kalẹ̀ nípa orúkọ mi tí a kò bá wà tàbí tí a bá fi kún nínú ìwé ìdásíwé àwọn èèyàn tí yóò lọ́wọ́?
answer: Lẹ́yìn tí ìwé ìdásíwé ti hàn, ẹnikẹ́ni lè gbé ìdájọ́ kalẹ̀ láàárín ọjọ́ 14 lẹ́yìn tí ìwé ìdásíwé ti hàn. Ìdájọ́ yẹn gbọ́dọ̀ wá láti inú fọ́rmù tí Ìjọba Ìṣọ̀kan ti ṣètò [act-s19-0].
src_question: How long do I have to raise an objection to my name being omitted or included in the voters' register?
src_answer: After the register is displayed, any person may raise an objection within 14 days of the display. The objection must be submitted on the form prescribed by the Commission [act-s19-0].

question: Ta ni lè gbọ́ ẹ̀bẹ̀ mi nípa orúkọ tí kò sí lórí àtòjọ àwọn olùdájọ́?
answer: Àjọ Ìṣọ̀kan Àwọn Olùdájọ́ (INEC) lè yan Olùṣàkóso Àtúnṣe láti gbọ́ àti pinnu ẹ̀bẹ̀ àti ìdàhùn nípa àwọn ìtẹ̀jáde tàbí ìyọkúrò nínú àtòjọ àkọ́kọ́ àwọn olùdájọ́. Olùṣàkóso yìí lè tún yan àwọn alágbàṣe bí ó bá wù [act-s20-0].
src_question: Who can hear my claim about a missing name on the voters list?
src_answer: The Commission may appoint a Revision Officer to hear and determine claims and objections about entries in or omissions from the preliminary list of voters. This officer can also appoint assistants as needed [act-s20-0].

question: Báwo ni mo ṣe le ṣe àtúnṣe sí ìpinnu Olùṣàkóso Àtúnṣe?
answer: Bí ẹnikẹ́ni bá kò fẹ́ràn ìpinnu Olùṣàkóso Àtúnṣe, ó lè ṣe àtúnṣe sí i lábẹ́ ọ̀sẹ̀ méje sí Olùṣàkóso Àwọn Ẹ̀ka Ìdìbò fún Ìpínlẹ̀ náà. Ìpinnu Olùṣàkóso Àwọn Ẹ̀ka Ìdìbò ni ó máa ń jẹ́ ìpinnu tí ó kẹ́hìn lábẹ́ òfin [act-s20-0].
src_question: If I disagree with the Revision Officer's decision, where can I appeal and is the decision final?
src_answer: If a person is dissatisfied with the Revision Officer's determination, they may appeal within seven days to the Resident Electoral Commissioner for that State. The Resident Electoral Commissioner's decision is final under the Act [act-s20-0].

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ tí ènìyàn lè gba fún kíkọ́ àkọ́lé ìwé ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ olùdìbò ní orúkọ ẹlòmíràn?
answer: Lábẹ́ Ìpín 23(1)(b) ti Ìwé Ìṣèjọba Ìdìbò, 2026, ìwé ìṣèjọba yìí jẹ́ ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí ó ní ìdájọ́ tí ó lè jẹ́ ìdájọ́ tí kò tó N100,000 tàbí ìdájọ́ ìgbà tí kò tó ọdún kan, tàbí méjèèjì [act-s23-0].
src_question: What punishment can a person receive for signing a voter registration form in someone else's name?
src_answer: Under Section 23(1)(b) of the Electoral Act, 2026, this act is an offence liable to a fine not more than N100,000 or imprisonment for a term not more than one year, or both [act-s23-0].

question: Kí ni àwọn ìdájọ́ fún àwọn tó ń ṣe àbẹ̀rù àwọn olùdìbò láti dẹ́kun wọn láti forúkọsílẹ̀?
answer: Ìpín 23(2)(a) sọ pé kí o ṣe tàbí kí o mú kí ènìyàn máa forúkọsílẹ̀ nípa ìdájọ́ tàbí ìdájọ́ ni ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ tí a lè fi ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ N500,000 tàbí ìdájọ́ fún ọdún mẹ́fà tàbí kò tó [act-s23-0].
src_question: What are the penalties for threatening voters to stop them from registering?
src_answer: Section 23(2)(a) states that causing or inducing persons to refrain from registering by duress is an offence punishable with a fine not more than N500,000 or imprisonment for a term not more than five years [act-s23-0].

question: Kí ni Ìjọba Àgbà lè ṣe bí ìjàmbá bá ṣeé ṣeé ṣe láti mú ìdìbò wáyé ní ọjọ́ tí a ti ṣètò?
answer: Gẹ́gẹ́ bí Ìpín 24(2) ṣe sọ, Ìjọba Àgbà lè tún ìdìbò náà padà, kí ó sì yàn ọjọ́ mìíràn fún ìdìbò tí a ti tún padà, bí ó bá jẹ́ pé ìdí tí a fi tún padà jẹ́ ìdí tí a lè gbà, tí a sì lè fi hàn [act-s24-0].
src_question: What can the Commission do if an emergency makes it impossible to hold an election on the scheduled date?
src_answer: According to Section 24(2), the Commission may postpone the election and appoint another date for the holding of the postponed election, provided the reason for the postponement is cogent and verifiable [act-s24-0].

question: Nígbà wo ni a lè sọ àwọn èsì ìdìbò lẹ́yìn ìdìbò tí a ti tún padà?
answer: Ìpín 24(4) sọ pé kò sí ìdájọ́ fún ìdìbò títí ìdìbò yóò fi wáyé ní agbègbè tí a ti yàn lẹ́yìn ọjọ́ tí a ti yàn [act-s24-0].
src_question: When can election results be declared after a postponed election?
src_answer: Section 24(4) specifies that there shall be no return for the election until polling has taken place in the area concerned after the substituted date [act-s24-0].

question: Ta ni o ni iduro fun ikede esi idibo ni ẹka idibo?
answer: Ẹsẹ 25(1)(a) sọ pe Olori Ẹka ni yoo ṣe ikede esi idibo [act-s25-0].
src_question: Who is responsible for announcing election results at the polling unit?
src_answer: Section 25(1)(a) states that the Presiding Officer at the polling unit shall announce the results of the election [act-s25-0].

question: Nibo ni Oludari Idibo yoo ṣe ikede olubori fun idibo Aṣofin?
answer: Lẹsẹkẹsẹ Ẹsẹ 25(2)(g), Oludari Idibo yoo ṣe ikede olubori ni Ẹka Idibo Ipinlẹ fun idibo Aṣofin [act-s25-0].
src_question: At which collation centre does the returning officer declare the winner for a Presidential election?
src_answer: Under Section 25(2)(g), the returning officer declares the winner at the State Collation Centre for a Presidential election [act-s25-0].

question: Kí ni àwọn alágbàṣe idibo gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe ṣáájú kí wọ́n tó kópa nínú idibo?
answer: Ẹsẹ 26(1) ń fún gbogbo àwọn alágbàṣe idibo, àwọn olùṣọ́, àwọn olori ẹka, àwọn oludari idibo, àti àwọn olùṣọ́ ààbò láti jẹ́ kí wọ́n jẹ́rìí tàbí kí wọ́n gbà àdúrà láti jẹ́ kí wọ́n jẹ́ aláìní ìdájọ́ àti aláìní ìdájọ́, kí wọ́n má ṣe gba ẹ̀bùn tàbí ẹ̀bùn, àti kí wọ́n ṣe iṣẹ́ wọn pẹ̀lú ìdájọ́ [act-s26-0].
src_question: What must election officials do before taking part in an election?
src_answer: Section 26(1) requires all staff, electoral officers, presiding officers, returning officers and security officials to affirm or swear to an oath of loyalty and neutrality as in the Second Schedule, not accept bribe or gratification, and perform duties impartially [act-s26-0].

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ fún alákóso ìdìbò tó bá ṣẹ́gun ìwàdà aláìṣàkóso?
answer: Ìpín 26(2) sọ pé ẹni tó bá ṣẹ́gun ìwàdà aláìṣàkóso nínú ìwàdà ìdìbò, ó máa ṣe ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí a máa fi ìdájọ́ sílẹ̀ lábẹ́ Ìpín 124 nínú Òfin yìí [act-s26-0].
src_question: What is the penalty for an election official who violates the oath of neutrality?
src_answer: Section 26(2) says that a person who violates subsection (1) commits an offence punishable under section 124 of this Act [act-s26-0].

question: Ta ni a kò gbọdọ̀ fi sí iṣẹ́ alákóso ìdìbò lábẹ́ Òfin Ìdìbò, 2026?
answer: Ẹni tí ó jẹ́ ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú tàbí tí ó ti fi ìfẹ́ hàn fún ẹni kankan láìsí ìdájọ́ kò gbọdọ̀ jẹ́ alákóso ìdìbò. Ìlànà yìí wà nínú Ìpín 27(1) nínú Òfin Ìdìbò, 2026 [act-s27-0].
src_question: Who is prohibited from being appointed as an election officer under the Electoral Act, 2026?
src_answer: No person who is a member of a political party or who has openly expressed support for any candidate shall be appointed as an election officer. This rule is in Section 27(1) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s27-0].

question: Ẹgbẹ́ ìjàbọ̀ wo ni Ìjọba lè béèrè láti fi dáàbò bo àwọn ohun èlò ìdìbò àti àwọn alákóso ìdìbò?
answer: Ìjọba lè béèrè fún ìdásílẹ̀ Ìjọba Àgbà Nàìjíríà láti fi dáàbò bo àwọn ohun èlò ìdìbò àti àwọn alákóso ìdìbò. Ìlànà yìí wà nínú Ìpín 27(3) nínú Òfin Ìdìbò, 2026 [act-s27-0].
src_question: Which security forces may the Commission request for deployment to protect election materials and officials?
src_answer: The Commission shall only request for the deployment of the Nigerian Armed Forces for the purpose of securing the distribution and delivery of election materials and protection of election officials. This is stated in Section 27(3) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s27-0].

question: Báwo ló ṣe ń jẹ́ kí INEC ṣe ìfihàn ìkìlọ̀ ìdìbò nígbà tí wọ́n ń ṣe ìdìbò gbogbogbò?
answer: INEC gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe ìfihàn ìkìlọ̀ ìdìbò láìpẹ́ ju ọjọ́ 300 ṣáájú ọjọ́ tí wọ́n ti yàn fún ìdìbò lọ. Ìbéèrè yìí wà nínú Ìwé Ìṣàkóso Ìdìbò, 2026, Ìwé 28(1) [act-s28-0].
src_question: How many days before a general election must the Commission publish the notice of election?
src_answer: The Commission must publish the notice not later than 300 days before the day appointed for holding the election. This requirement is in Section 28(1) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s28-0].

question: Nígbà wo ló gbọ́dọ̀ fi àkójọ àwọn olùdìbò tí ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú kan gbé kalẹ̀ fún ìdìbò gbogbogbò?
answer: Gbogbo ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú gbọ́dọ̀ fi àkójọ àwọn olùdìbò wọn kalẹ̀ láì pọ̀ ju ọjọ́ mẹ́rìndínlógún (120) ṣáájú ọjọ́ tí a yàn fún ìdìbò gbogbogbò. Èyí ni a ti sọ nínú Ìwé-òfin Ìdìbò, 2026, Ìpín 29(1) [act-s29-0].
src_question: Within what timeframe must a political party submit its list of candidates for a general election?
src_answer: Every political party must submit the list of candidates not later than 120 days before the date appointed for a general election. This is set out in Section 29(1) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s29-0].

question: Kí ni ìwé tí ó gbọ́dọ̀ wà pẹ̀lú àtòjọ àwọn olùdìbò tí ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú kan fi ṣàkóso?
answer: Àtòjọ náà gbọ́dọ̀ wà pẹ̀lú ìwé ìfẹ̀hónúhàn tí a ti gbàdúrà ní ilé-ẹjọ́ gíga, ilé-ẹjọ́ ìpínlẹ̀, tàbí Ìlú Ìjọba Àpapọ̀, tí ó sọ pé olùdìbò náà ti ṣe gbogbo àwọn ìbéèrè òfin. Ìbéèrè yìí wà nínú Ìwé Òfin Ìdìbò, 2026, Ìwé 29(2) [act-s29-0].
src_question: What document must accompany the list of candidates submitted by a political party?
src_answer: The list must be accompanied by an affidavit sworn to by the candidate at the Federal High Court, High Court of a State, or Federal Capital Territory, indicating that the candidate has fulfilled all constitutional requirements. This requirement is in Section 29(2) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s29-0].

question: Bí ilé-ẹjọ́ bá rí i pé ìwé ìfẹ̀hónúhàn olùdìbò kan ní àlàyé àìtọ́ nípa ìyè òfin, kí ni èsì?
answer: Ilé-ẹjọ́ yóò fún olùdìbò náà àti ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú tí ó ń ṣe àtìlẹ́yìn rẹ̀ ní ìdájọ́ láti máa ṣe ìdìbò. Ìwé Òfin Ìdìbò, 2026, Ìwé 29(6) [act-s29-1].
src_question: If a court finds that a candidate's affidavit contains false information about constitutional eligibility, what is the consequence?
src_answer: The court shall issue an order disqualifying the candidate and the sponsoring political party. This provision is in Section 29(6) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s29-1].

question: Kí ni adirẹsi tí olùdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ fún nígbà tí ó bá ń fi fọọmu ìdìbò tí a ti ṣàkóso ṣàkóso?
answer: Olùdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ fún adirẹsi tí a lè mọ̀ ní ìpínlẹ̀ tí ó fẹ́ láti ṣe ìdìbò, tí gbogbo àwọn ìwé àti ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ ilé-ẹjọ́ yóò wà níbẹ̀. Ìbéèrè yìí wà nínú Ìwé Òfin Ìdìbò, 2026, Ìwé 29(8) [act-s29-1].
src_question: What address must a candidate provide when submitting the prescribed nomination form?
src_answer: The candidate must furnish an identifiable address in the state where he or she intends to contest the election, at which all documents and court processes shall be served. This requirement is in Section 29(8) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s29-1].

question: Kí ni àwọn ìbéèrè fún ìdásílẹ̀ olùdásílẹ̀ fún ìdìbò?
answer: Olùdásílẹ̀ gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ ìdásílẹ̀ ní kíkà nípa àwọn ènìyàn tí orúkọ wọn wà lórí ìwé ìṣàkóso àwọn ènìyàn ní agbègbè ìdìbò gẹ́gẹ́ bí Ìjọba Ìṣàkóso ṣe lè ṣàlàyé [act-s30-0]. Ẹni kò gbọ́dọ̀ dásílẹ̀ ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ènìyàn fún ọ̀kan nìkan [act-s30-0].
src_question: What are the requirements for nominating a candidate for an election?
src_answer: A candidate must be nominated in writing by such number of persons whose names appear on the register of voters in the constituency as the Commission may prescribe [act-s30-0]. A person may not nominate more than one person for the same office [act-s30-0].

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ fún ìdásílẹ̀ ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ènìyàn fún ọ̀kan nìkan?
answer: Ẹni tí ó bá dásílẹ̀ ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ènìyàn fún ọ̀kan nìkan ń ṣe ẹ̀ṣẹ̀, ó sì lè ní ìdájọ́ láti ní owó tí kò tó N100,000 tàbí ìdájọ́ ìgbà mẹ́ta oṣù tàbí méjèèjì [act-s30-0]. Ṣùgbọ́n, ìdásílẹ̀ kò ní di àìṣe [act-s30-0].
src_question: What is the penalty for nominating more than one person for the same office?
src_answer: A person who nominates more than one person for the same office commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not more than N100,000 or imprisonment for a term of three months or both [act-s30-0]. However, the nomination is not invalidated by such action [act-s30-0].

question: Kí ni iye ìwọ̀n tí agbègbè ìjọba àgbègbè gbọ́dọ̀ ní?
answer: Ìjọba Ìṣàkóso yóò pín agbègbè ìjọba àgbègbè sí àwọn agbègbè ìdìbò tàbí àwọn ìdìbò kò gbọ́dọ̀ kéré ju 10 gẹ́gẹ́ bí àwọn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ ṣe lè nílò [act-s40-0]. Nítorí náà, agbègbè ìjọba àgbègbè gbọ́dọ̀ ní ọgọ́rùn-ún ìdìbò.
src_question: What is the minimum number of electoral wards that a Local Government Area must have?
src_answer: The Commission shall divide each Local Government Area into registration areas or Electoral Wards not being less than 10 as the circumstances may require [act-s40-0]. Therefore, a Local Government Area must have at least ten wards.

question: Ta ni ṣe ipinnu iye awọn ẹka-ọṣuwọn ti a ṣeto ni agbegbe kan?
answer: Ẹka yoo ṣeto iye to peye ti awọn ẹka-ọṣuwọn ni agbegbe kọọkan tabi Ẹka-Ọṣuwọn [act-s40-0]. Ẹka tun pin awọn oludibo si awọn ẹka-ọṣuwọn wọnyi [act-s40-0].
src_question: Who decides how many polling units are set up in a registration area?
src_answer: The Commission shall establish an adequate number of polling units in each registration area or Electoral Ward [act-s40-0]. The Commission also allots voters to those polling units [act-s40-0].

question: Kini awọn ẹrọ ti a le lo fun idibo?
answer: Ẹka yoo pese awọn apoti, ẹrọ idibo ẹlẹktrọniku tabi ẹrọ idibo miiran fun ṣiṣe idibo [act-s41-0]. Awọn fọọmu pataki ti a le lo ni Ẹka yoo pinnu [act-s41-0].
src_question: What voting devices may be used for elections?
src_answer: The Commission shall provide suitable boxes, electronic voting machine or any other voting device for the conduct of elections [act-s41-0]. The specific forms to be used are determined by the Commission [act-s41-0].

question: Ṣe awọn oludibo le wo awọn ohun elo idibo ṣaaju ki idibo bẹrẹ?
answer: Awọn oludibo ti o wa ni ẹka-ọṣuwọn le wo awọn ohun elo idibo atilẹba ṣaaju ki idibo bẹrẹ [act-s41-0]. Wọn le kọ eyi ni iwe, lori fidio tabi ni ọna miiran [act-s41-0].
src_question: Can polling agents inspect the electoral materials before voting begins?
src_answer: Polling agents who are in attendance at a polling unit may inspect originals of the electoral materials before the commencement of the election [act-s41-0]. They may record this inspection as evidence in writing, on video or by other means [act-s41-0].

question: Báwo ló ṣe ń lọ nípa ìgbà tí INEC gbọ́dọ̀ pe àwọn ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú láti ṣàyẹ̀wò orúkọ wọn lórí àwọn ìwé ìdìbò?
answer: INEC gbọ́dọ̀, kò gbọ́dọ̀ ju ọjọ́ ọgọ́ta (60) ṣáájú ìdìbò, fi ìwé ránṣẹ́ sí ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú tí ó gbé olúborí kalẹ̀ láti ṣàyẹ̀wò orúkọ wọn lórí àwọn àpẹẹrẹ ìwé ìdìbò . Ẹgbẹ́ náà ní ọjọ́ méjì láti fọwọ́ sí tàbí kọ orúkọ wọn ní ìwé . [act-s42-0]
src_question: How many days before an election must the Commission invite political parties to inspect their identity on ballot papers?
src_answer: The Commission shall, not later than 60 days to an election, invite in writing a political party that nominated a candidate to inspect its identity on samples of electoral materials [act-s42-0]. The party then has two days to approve or disapprove its identity in writing [act-s42-0].

question: Kí ni tó má ṣẹlẹ bí ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú bá kò dáhùn ìbéèrè ìjọba láti ṣàyẹ̀wò ìdánimọ̀ wọn?
answer: Bí ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú bá kò bá ìbéèrè ìjọba mu, wọ́n á gbà pé wọ́n ti fọwọ́ sí ìdánimọ̀ wọn lórí àwọn ohun èlò ìdìbò tí a gbèrò fún ìdìbò [act-s42-0]. Nítorí náà, ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú kò lè béèrè pé wọ́n kò ṣe ìyàtọ̀ fún wọn nítorí ìdánimọ̀ wọn [act-s42-0].
src_question: What happens if a political party does not respond to the Commission's invitation to inspect its identity?
src_answer: If a political party fails to comply with the invitation, it shall be deemed to have approved its identity on samples of electoral materials proposed for the election [act-s42-0]. Consequently, the party cannot later complain of unlawful exclusion based on its identity [act-s42-0].

question: Kí ni gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe láti yàn àgbà ìdìbò fún ẹ̀ka ìdìbò kan?
answer: Àgbà ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ fúnni ní ìfọ̀rọ̀wérọ̀ ní kíkà sí Alákóso Ìdìbò Ìjọba Ìpínlẹ̀ tí ó ní orúkọ, adírẹ́sì àti àwọn ìròyìn ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ rẹ̀. Ìfọ̀rọ̀wérọ̀ náà gbọ́dọ̀ ní àwọn fọ́tò ìwé-ẹ̀rí ìdánilójú méjì àti àpẹẹrẹ àmì-ẹ̀rọ àgbà ìdìbò, tí a gbọ́dọ̀ fúnni sí ọ̀gá ìdìbò ní ìgbà tí ó tó ọjọ́ 14 ṣáájú ọjọ́ ìdìbò [act-s43-0].
src_question: What must a candidate submit to appoint a polling agent for a polling unit?
src_answer: The candidate must give a notice in writing addressed to the Resident Electoral Commissioner of the State that includes the polling agent’s name, address and contact details. The notice must be accompanied by two passport photographs and a sample signature of the polling agent and be given to the electoral officer at least 14 days before the election date [act-s43-0].

question: Kí ni àwọn olùṣèlú tí kò gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ olùṣàkóso ìdìbò àyàfi bí wọ́n bá fi ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ sílẹ̀ mẹ́ta oṣù ṣáájú ìdìbò?
answer: Ẹni tí ó ń ṣiṣẹ́ gẹ́gẹ́ bí Ààrẹ tàbí ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ Ìjọba Ìbílẹ̀ tàbí Ìgbìmọ̀ Ìjọba Ìbílẹ̀, Alákòóso, Ààrẹ Ìgbìmọ̀ Aṣòfin Ìpínlẹ̀, Ààrẹ Ìgbìmọ̀ Aṣòfin Ìpínlẹ̀, Tóun Tóun Ìjọba Àpapọ̀, tàbí ẹni míì tí ó ń gbé ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ ìṣèlú tàbí ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ ìyàn lábẹ́ ẹ̀ka ìjọba kọ̀ọ̀kan, kò gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ olùṣàkóso ìdìbò. Ó lè ṣiṣẹ́ nìkan bí ó bá ti fi ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ sílẹ̀ láti ọ̀dọ̀ rẹ̀ mẹ́ta oṣù ṣáájú ìdìbò [act-s43-0].
src_question: Which public officials are not allowed to serve as polling agents unless they resign three months before the election?
src_answer: A person who is serving as Chairman or member of a Local Government Area or Area Council, Commissioner, Deputy Governor or Governor of a State, Minister of the Federal Government, or any other person holding elective or appointive political office under any tier of government is prohibited from serving as a polling agent. He may serve only if he has resigned from his office at least three months prior to the election [act-s43-0].

question: Bí olùṣàkóso ìdìbò bá kò bá lọ sí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí òfin ṣe pàṣẹ, ṣé ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ náà yóò di aláìlẹ́ṣẹ̀?
answer: Kò ṣeé ṣe kí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ náà di aláìlẹ́ṣẹ̀ bí olùṣàkóso ìdìbò bá kò bá lọ sí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí òfin ṣe pàṣẹ ní àkókò àti ibi tí a ti yàn fún un, bí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ náà bá ti ṣe déédéé. Ìyẹn náà ni yóò ṣẹlẹ̀ bí olùṣàkóso ìdìbò bá kò bá fẹ́ ṣe ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ náà, bí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ náà bá ti ṣe déédéé [act-s43-1].
src_question: If a polling agent does not attend an act required by the Act, does that invalidate the act?
src_answer: The non‑attendance of the Polling Agent at the time and place appointed for the act does not invalidate the act if the act is otherwise done properly. The same applies if the Polling Agent refuses to do the act, provided the act is performed correctly [act-s43-1].

question: Kí ni ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ bí olùṣàkóso ìdìbò bá kò bá ṣe ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí òfin ṣe pàṣẹ?
answer: Bí olùṣàkóso ìdìbò bá kò bá ṣe ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí òfin ṣe pàṣẹ, ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ náà kò ní di aláìlẹ́ṣẹ̀. Ìyẹn yóò wà ní títí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ náà bá ti ṣe déédéé ní ọwọ́ ẹlòmìíràn [act-s43-1].
src_question: What is the effect if a polling agent refuses to perform an act that the Act requires?
src_answer: If a polling agent refuses to perform an act required by the Act, the act is not invalidated. This holds as long as the act is performed correctly by someone else [act-s43-1].

question: Kí ni àwọn ìgbésẹ̀ tí Olùdarí Ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe pẹ̀lú àpótí ìdìbò ṣáájú ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ ìdìbò?
answer: Ní àkókò tí a ti ṣètò fún ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ ìdìbò, Olùdarí Ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ ṣí àpótí ìdìbò tí kò ní ẹ̀rù tàbí fi ẹ̀rọ ìdìbò hàn sí àwọn ènìyàn tí wọ́n wà níbẹ̀. Lẹ́yìn náà, ó gbọ́dọ̀ pa àpótí náà mọ́ àti fi àmúṣe sí i ní ọ̀nà tí ó máa dènà ẹnikẹ́ni láti ṣí i láìsí ìyànjú [act-s46-0].
src_question: What steps must the Presiding Officer take with the ballot box before voting begins?
src_answer: At the hour fixed for opening the poll, the Presiding Officer must open the empty ballot box or present the voting device and show it to persons lawfully present. He must then close and seal the box in a manner that prevents it from being opened by any unauthorised person [act-s46-0].

question: Níbi wo ni àpótí ìdìbò tí a ti fi àmúṣe sí gbọ́dọ̀ wà nígbà ìdìbò?
answer: Àpótí ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ wà ní ìwòye gbogbo àwọn tí wọ́n wà níbẹ̀. Ó gbọ́dọ̀ wà ní ipò yẹn títí ìdìbò yóò fi parí [act-s46-0].
src_question: Where must the sealed ballot box be kept during the voting period?
src_answer: The ballot box shall be placed in full view of all present. It must be kept in that condition until the close of poll [act-s46-0].

question: Kí ni olùdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ fi hàn láti jẹ́ kí wọ́n gba wọ́n gẹ́gẹ́ bí olùdìbò ṣáájú ìdìbò?
answer: Olùdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ fi ara rẹ̀ hàn sí Olùdarí Ìdìbò fún ìgbàkẹyìn ní ibi ìdìbò ní agbègbè tí orúkọ rẹ̀ wà lórí ìwé ìdìbò. Ó gbọ́dọ̀ tún fi ìwé ìdìbò olùdìbò (PVC) rẹ̀ hàn [act-s47-0].
src_question: What must a voter present to be accredited before voting?
src_answer: The voter must present himself to a Presiding Officer for accreditation at the polling unit in the constituency where his name is registered. He must also provide his permanent voters card (PVC) [act-s47-0].

question: Kí ni yóò ṣẹlẹ̀ bí Bimodal Voter Accreditation System bá ṣubú ní ibi ìdìbò kan, tí kò sí ẹ̀rọ ìdásíwé?
answer: Bí Bimodal Voter Accreditation System tàbí ẹ̀rọ ìdásíwé míì bá ṣubú ní ibi ìdìbò kan, tí kò sí ẹ̀rọ tuntun, ìdìbò nínú ibi yẹn yóò jẹ́ kí a pa. Ẹ̀ka yóò lè ṣe ìdìbò mìíràn nínú ọjọ́ 24, ṣùgbọ́n nìkan bí wọ́n bá rí i pé èsì ìdìbò nínú ibi yẹn yóò ní ipa pàtàkì lórí èsì ìdìbò gbogbo àti ìdásílẹ̀ olórí nínú agbègbè yẹn [act-s47-0].
src_question: What happens if the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System fails at a polling unit and no replacement device is provided?
src_answer: If the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System or any other technological device fails in a polling unit and a fresh card reader or technological device is not deployed, the election in that unit shall be cancelled. The Commission may then schedule another election within 24 hours, but only if it is satisfied that the result of the election in that polling unit will substantially affect the final result of the whole election and declaration of a winner in the constituency concerned [act-s47-0].

question: Báwo ni mo ṣe gbọ́dọ̀ fi ìdìbò mi sílẹ̀ gẹ́gẹ́ bí Ìwé Ìdìbò ṣe sọ?
answer: Ìdìbò yóò jẹ́ nípa ìdìbò ìṣekúse, àti pé olùdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ fi ìdìbò rẹ̀ sílẹ̀ ní ọ̀nà tí Ẹ̀ka ti ṣàlàyé. Gbogbo ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ wá sí inú ìdìbò nínú ibi tí gbogbo ènìyàn lè rí. Èyí ni a nílò lábẹ́ Ìwé Ìdìbò, 2026, Ìpín 50 [act-s50-0].
src_question: How must I cast my vote according to the Electoral Act?
src_answer: Voting at an election shall be by open secret ballot, and a voter must mark the ballot paper in the manner prescribed by the Commission. All ballots must be deposited in the ballot box in the open view of the public. This is required by section 50 of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s50-0].

question: Ta ni ó pinnu ìlànà ìdìbò fún ìdìbò?
answer: Ẹ̀ka ni ó pinnu ìlànà ìdìbò àti ìtẹ̀jáde èsì, lábẹ́ Ìwé Ìdìbò, 2026, Ìpín 60. Ìlànà yìí wà nínú Ìpín 50, Ìpín 2 [act-s50-0].
src_question: Who decides the voting procedure for elections?
src_answer: The Commission determines the procedure for voting and transmission of results, subject to section 60 of this Act. This rule is set out in subsection (2) of section 50 of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s50-0].

question: Ṣé mo lè fi ọwọ́ kan ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn olùdìbò ní ìdìbò kan?
answer: Rárá, olùdìbò kò gbọ́dọ̀ fi ọwọ́ kan ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn olùdìbò tàbí kọ́ ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ìdìbò fún olùdìbò kankan ní ìdìbò kan. Ìdènà yìí wà nínú ìsọ̀rọ̀ (1) ti ìwé ìdìbò 51 ti Ìwé Ìdìbò, 2026 [act-s51-0].
src_question: Can I vote for more than one candidate in an election?
src_answer: No, a voter shall not vote for more than one candidate or record more than one vote in favour of any candidate at any one election. This prohibition is stated in subsection (1) of section 51 of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s51-0].

question: Kí ni yóò ṣẹlẹ̀ bí ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ ìdìbò bá wá láti ọwọ́ àwọn olùdìbò ní ẹ̀ka ìdìbò mi?
answer: Bí iye ìdìbò tí a kọ́ bá lé ewu iye àwọn olùdìbò tí a gbà, Olùdarí Ìdìbò yóò pa èsì ìdìbò náà nínú ẹ̀ka ìdìbò yẹn. Ìbéèrè yìí wà nínú ìsọ̀rọ̀ (2) ti ìwé ìdìbò 51 ti Ìwé Ìdìbò, 2026 [act-s51-0].
src_question: What happens if more votes are cast in my polling unit than the number of accredited voters?
src_answer: If the number of votes cast exceeds the number of accredited voters, the Presiding Officer shall cancel the result of the election in that polling unit. This requirement is found in subsection (2) of section 51 of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s51-0].

question: Ṣé ìdìbò mi yóò jẹ́ kíkọ́ lára bí mo bá ní àmì ọwọ́ láti inú ìdáná tí a lò ní ibi ìdìbò?
answer: Rárá, èyíkéyìí àmì tí ó wá láti inú ìdáná tí a fi sí ọwọ́ olùdìbò nínú àpótí ìdìbò kò gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ tàbí jẹ́ ìdánimọ̀ lábẹ́ ìwé ìdìbò yìí. Nítorí náà, àmì ọwọ́ kò ní fa kí ìdìbò kò gba. Ìlànà yìí wà nínú ìsọ̀rọ̀ (1) ti ìwé ìdìbò 52 ti Ìwé Ìdìbò, 2026 [act-s52-0].
src_question: Will my ballot be rejected if I have a thumb stain from the ink used at the polling station?
src_answer: No, any print resulting from the staining of the thumb of the voter in the voting compartment shall not be or be deemed to be a mark of identification under this section. Therefore a thumb stain does not cause rejection of the ballot paper. This rule is in subsection (1) of section 52 of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s52-0].

question: Kí ni irú àwòrán tí Ìjọba gbọ́dọ̀ lo fún àmì ọwọ́ lórí àwọn ìwé ìdìbò?
answer: Ìjọba gbọ́dọ̀ lo àwòrán tí kò ní yí padà fún àmì ọwọ́ àwọn olùdìbò lórí àwọn ìwé ìdìbò. Ìbéèrè yìí wà nínú ìsọ̀kan (2) ti ìwé ìṣọ̀kan 52 ti Ìwé Ìdìbò, 2026 [act-s52-0].
src_question: What type of ink must the Commission use for thumb marks on ballot papers?
src_answer: The Commission shall use indelible ink for any thumb mark by voters on ballot papers. This requirement is stated in subsection (2) of section 52 of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s52-0].

question: Kí ni mo gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe bí mo bá ṣe pa ìwé ìdìbò mi lọ́fẹ̀ẹ́?
answer: O lè fi ìwé ìdìbò tí o ti pa lọ sí Olùdarí Ìdìbò; bí Olùdarí Ìdìbò bá rí i pé ìwé ìdìbò náà ti pa lọ, ó gbọ́dọ̀ fún ọ ní ìwé ìdìbò tuntun dipo tí o fi lọ, àti pé ìwé ìdìbò tí o ti pa lọ gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ kí a mọ̀ pé a ti pa a lọ. Ìlànà yìí wà nínú ìwé ìṣọ̀kan 53 ti Ìwé Ìdìbò, 2026 [act-s53-0].
src_question: What should I do if I accidentally damage my ballot paper?
src_answer: You may deliver the spoilt ballot paper to the Presiding Officer; if the Presiding Officer is satisfied that the ballot paper is spoilt, he or she shall issue another ballot paper to you in place of the one delivered, and the spoilt ballot paper shall be immediately marked cancelled. This procedure is set out in section 53 of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s53-0].

question: Ta ni ó pinnu bóyá ìwé ìdìbò kan ti pa lọ àti pé a lè fi tuntun rọ̀pò rẹ̀?
answer: Olùdarí Ìdìbò ni ó pinnu bóyá ìwé ìdìbò kan ti pa lọ, lẹ́yìn náà ó gbọ́dọ̀ fún ọ ní ìwé ìdìbò tuntun àti pé ó gbọ́dọ̀ fi àmì kan sí ìwé ìdìbò tí o ti pa lọ láti jẹ́ kí a mọ̀ pé a ti pa a lọ. Ìyẹn ni ìyàtọ̀ tí Ìwé Ìdìbò, 2026 [act-s53-0] ṣe sọ.
src_question: Who decides whether a ballot paper is spoilt and can be replaced?
src_answer: The Presiding Officer decides if satisfied that the ballot paper is spoilt, then issues a new ballot paper and marks the original cancelled. This authority is given by section 53 of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s53-0].

question: Ta ni o ni iduro fun fifiranṣẹ awọn abajade idibo lẹyin ti wọn ti ṣe ikede?
answer: Gẹgẹ bi Apakan 62(1) ti Ofin Idibo, 2026 [act-s62-0], Oludari Idibo ni o ni iduro lati fi awọn abajade ti a ti kọ silẹ pẹlu awọn ohun elo idibo ti a fi aabo pamọ si ẹni ti a ti yan nipasẹ Ẹka. Fifiranṣẹ gbọdọ ni awọn oludije tabi awọn aṣoju wọn nibikibi ti wọn ba wa.
src_question: Who is responsible for delivering the election results after they are announced?
src_answer: According to Section 62(1) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s62-0], the Presiding Officer must deliver the recorded result together with election materials under security to the person prescribed by the Commission. The delivery must be accompanied by the candidates or their polling agents where available.

question: Bawo ni oludibo le ri ẹri ti a fọwọsi ti awọn abajade idibo lati iwe-ẹri orilẹ-ede?
answer: Apakan 62(3) ti Ofin Idibo, 2026 [act-s62-0] sọ pe ẹnikẹni tabi ẹgbẹ oṣelu le ri ẹri ti o tọ ti awọn abajade idibo ti a fi pamọ si iwe-ẹri orilẹ-ede nipasẹ sisan owo-ori ti Ẹka ti ṣeto. Ẹri naa le wa ni fọọmu ti a tẹ tabi ti o wa lori ẹrọ ati pe o le bo awọn abajade fun ipinlẹ, Ijọba Agbegbe, Ijọba Agbegbe, agbegbe idibo, tabi ẹka idibo.
src_question: How can a voter obtain a certified copy of election results from the National Electronic Register?
src_answer: Section 62(3) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s62-0] states that any person or political party may obtain a certified true copy of any election result kept in the National Electronic Register by paying the fees set by the Commission. The copy may be in printed or electronic format and can cover results for a State, Local Government, Area Council, registration area, Electoral Ward or Polling Unit.

question: Kini ohun ti oludamọran gbọdọ ṣayẹwo ṣaaju ki o to ṣe ikede awọn abajade idibo?
answer: Apakan 62(4) ti Ofin Idibo, 2026 [act-s62-1] nilo ki oludamọran ṣayẹwo pe nọmba awọn oludibo ti a fọwọsi lori abajade ti a ti ṣe idamọran ba nọmba ti a ti kọ silẹ labẹ apakan 47(2) ati ti a fi ranṣẹ lati awọn ẹka idibo, ati pe awọn idibo ti a sọ ba awọn idibo ti a kọ ati ti a fi ranṣẹ labẹ apakan 60(4). Lẹhin awọn ṣayẹwo wọnyi ni oludamọran le ṣe ikede abajade.
src_question: What must a collation officer verify before announcing election results?
src_answer: Section 62(4) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s62-1] requires the collation officer to verify that the number of accredited voters on the collated result matches the number recorded under section 47(2) and transmitted from polling units, and that the votes stated match the votes recorded and transmitted under section 60(4). Only after these checks may the officer announce the result.

question: Kí ni àwọn nọ́mbà olùdìbò tí olùdarí ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ lo nígbà tí ó ń kà àwọn èsì?
answer: Lábẹ́ Ìpín 62(5) ti Òfin Ìdìbò, 2026 [act-s62-1], olùdarí ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ lo nọ́mbà àwọn olùdìbò tí a gbàṣẹ láti ìwé ìròyìn tí a kọ lábẹ́ Ìpín 47(2) tí a sì rán láti àwọn ẹ̀ka ìdìbò lábẹ́ Ìpín 60(5) láti kà àti sọ èsì jáde, bí èsì tí a kà ní ìpele rẹ̀ tàbí ìpele tí ó wà lábẹ́ rẹ̀ bá jẹ́ títọ́.
src_question: Which voter numbers must a returning officer use when collating results?
src_answer: Under Section 62(5) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s62-1], a returning officer must use the number of accredited voters recorded under section 47(2) and transmitted directly from polling units under section 60(5) to collate and announce the result, provided the collated result at his or a lower level is correct.

question: Kí ni àwọn ìwé tí olùdarí ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ ṣàyẹ̀wò nígbà tí ìjàǹbá bá wà lórí èsì ẹ̀ka ìdìbò?
answer: Ìpín 62(6) ti Òfin Ìdìbò, 2026 [act-s62-2] sọ pé olùdarí ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ ṣàyẹ̀wò èsì tí a kà ní ìjàǹbá, àwọn ìwé tí a rán láti ẹ̀rọ ìkàwé Smart Card tàbí ẹ̀rọ ìgbàṣẹ mìíràn, àwọn ìwé ìgbàṣẹ tí a kọ lábẹ́ Ìpín 47(2) tí a sì rán láti ẹ̀ka ìdìbò, àti àwọn ìdìbò àti èsì tí a kọ àti rán lábẹ́ Ìpín 60(5). Àwọn ìwé wọ̀nyí ni a fi ń ṣàyẹ̀wò bóyá èsì tí a kà ní ìjàǹbá jẹ́ títọ́.
src_question: What documents must a returning officer review when there is a dispute over a polling unit result?
src_answer: Section 62(6) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s62-2] states that the officer must review the original disputed collated result, the Smart Card Reader or other accreditation device data, the accreditation data recorded under section 47(2) and transmitted from the polling unit, and the votes and result recorded and transmitted under section 60(5). These items are used to determine the correctness of the disputed result.

question: Bí èsì ìdìbò tí a kà ní ìjàǹbá bá jẹ́ àìtọ́, kí ni olùdarí ìkà ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe?
answer: Gẹ́gẹ́ bí Ìpín 62(7) ti Òfin Ìdìbò, 2026 [act-s62-2] ṣe sọ, nígbà tí èsì tí a kà ní ìjàǹbá bá jẹ́ àìtọ́, olùdarí ìkà ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ tún kà èsì náà àti sọ èsì tuntun jáde pẹ̀lú àwọn ìwé tí a tọ́ka sí lábẹ́ Ìpín 62(6)(a) sí (d). Èyí ni yóò jẹ́ kí èsì tí ó kẹ́hìn jẹ́ títọ́.
src_question: If a disputed election result is found to be incorrect, what must the collation officer do?
src_answer: According to Section 62(7) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s62-2], when a disputed result is found incorrect, the collation officer must re-collate and announce a new result using the information listed in subsection (6)(a) through (d). This ensures the final result reflects the verified data.

question: Ṣé aṣẹ́ ìdìbò láìní àmì ìjọba lè wà ní ìṣirò nínú ìdìbò?
answer: Ìpín 63(2) ti Ìwé Ìṣèlú Ìdìbò, 2026 [act-s63-0] gba aṣẹ́ ìdìbò láìní àmì ìjọba láti wà ní ìṣirò bíi tí olùdarí ìdìbò bá ṣàkíyèsí pé ó wá láti inú ìwé aṣẹ́ ìdìbò tí a fún Olùdarí Ìdìbò ìlú ìdìbò náà. Ní àkókò yìí, àìní àmì ìjọba kò ní dènà ìṣirò ìdìbò.
src_question: Can a ballot paper without an official mark still be counted in an election?
src_answer: Section 63(2) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s63-0] allows a ballot paper without an official mark to be counted if the returning officer is satisfied that it came from a book of ballot papers furnished to the Presiding Officer of the polling unit for that election. In that case, the absence of the official mark does not prevent the vote from being counted.

question: Lábẹ́ àkókò wo ni aṣẹ́ ìdìbò láìní àmì ìjọba yóò wà ní ìṣirò?
answer: Ìpín 63(2) ti Ìwé Ìṣèlú Ìdìbò, 2026 [act-s63-0] sọ pé aṣẹ́ ìdìbò láìní àmì ìjọba yóò wà ní ìṣirò nìkan nígbà tí olùdarí ìdìbò bá ṣàkíyèsí pé ó wá láti inú ìwé aṣẹ́ ìdìbò tó tọ́ tí a fún Olùdarí Ìdìbò ìlú ìdìbò náà. Ìṣàkíyèsí yìí yóò pa ìdílé àmì ìjọba mọ́.
src_question: Under what condition is a ballot paper without an official mark counted?
src_answer: Section 63(2) of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s63-0] states that a ballot paper without an official mark shall be counted only when the returning officer confirms it originated from the correct book of ballot papers provided to the polling unit’s Presiding Officer for the election in question. This confirmation overrides the requirement for the official mark.

question: Kí ni Olùdarí Ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ kọ lórí aṣẹ́ ìdìbò tí a kọ̀?
answer: Olùdarí Ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ kọ ọ̀rọ̀ "kọ̀" lórí aṣẹ́ ìdìbò tí a kọ̀ lábẹ́ Ìpín 52(1) ti Ìwé Ìṣèlú Ìdìbò tàbí fún èyíkéyìí ìdí mìíràn. Aṣẹ́ ìdìbò kò ní wà ní ìṣirò bíi tí olùdarí ìdìbò bá yí ìṣàkíyèsí rẹ̀ padà láti gba aṣẹ́ náà [act-s64-0].
src_question: What must the Presiding Officer write on a ballot paper that is rejected?
src_answer: The Presiding Officer must endorse the word rejected on the ballot paper that is rejected under section 52(1) of the Act or for any other reason. The ballot papers shall not be counted unless the returning officer overrules the Presiding Officer and allows it [act-s64-0].

question: Kí ni gbọ́dọ̀ ṣẹlẹ̀ bí olúborí tàbí aláṣẹ ìdìbò bá ń bẹ̀rù pé àkójọ ìdìbò ti ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀ ṣàkóso?
answer: Bí olúborí tàbí aláṣẹ ìdìbò bá ń bẹ̀rù pé àkójọ ìdìbò ti ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀ ṣàkóso, Olùdarí Ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ ṣàfihàn àkójọ náà lórí àkójọ ìdìbò, ṣàfihàn pé ó ti ṣẹ̀ṣẹ̀ ṣàkóso, àti pé ó ti ṣàfihàn àwọn ìdáhùn tòótọ́ nípa ìṣàkóso náà. Ó gbọ́dọ̀ tún ṣàfihàn àwọn ìdáhùn tòótọ́ nípa àwọn ìṣàkóso tí ó wà lórí àkójọ náà, àti pé ó gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ kí olúborí tàbí aláṣẹ ìdìbò ṣe àtúnṣe àwọn ìdáhùn náà lórí àkójọ ìdìbò. [act-s64-0]
src_question: What must happen if a candidate or polling agent objects to a ballot paper being rejected?
src_answer: If a candidate or polling agent objects at the time the decision is made, the Presiding Officer must add the phrase but objected to after the word rejected on the ballot paper. The Presiding Officer must also prepare a statement listing the number of rejected papers, the reason for rejection and their serial numbers, and must allow the candidate or polling agent to copy that statement upon request [act-s64-0].

question: Báwo ló ṣe ń lọ fún INEC láti ṣàtúnṣe ìfihàn tàbí ìdàhùn lẹ́yìn tí wọ́n bá gba ìròyìn?
answer: INEC ní ọjọ́ méje láti ṣàtúnṣe ìfihàn àti ìdàhùn lẹ́yìn tí wọ́n bá gba ìròyìn láti ọwọ́ àwọn ọ̀gá wọn. Ìgbà yìí ni a ṣàlàyé nínú Ìwé-òfin Ìdìbò, 2026, Ìpín 65 [act-s65-0].
src_question: How much time does the Commission have to review a declaration or return after receiving a report?
src_answer: The Commission has seven days to review the declaration and return after it receives a report from its officials. This period is specified in Section 65 of the Electoral Act, 2026 [act-s65-0].

question: Báwo ni olúborí yóò jẹ́ alágbára nínú ìdìbò ààrẹ tàbí ìdìbò gómìnà gẹ́gẹ́ bí Ìwé-òfin Ìdìbò ṣe sọ?
answer: Nínú ìdìbò fún Ààrẹ tàbí Gómìnà, bóyá tí wọ́n bá ń ṣeré tàbí kò, èsì yóò jẹ́ láti kíkà àwọn ìdìbò tí a fi sílẹ̀ fún gbogbo àwọn olùdìbò. Olùdìbò tí ó gba ìdìbò púpọ̀ jù lọ ni yóò jẹ́ olúborí, gẹ́gẹ́ bí àwọn ìwé-òfin 133, 134, àti 179 ti Ìwé-òfin ṣe sọ [act-s66-0].
src_question: How is the winner determined in a presidential or gubernatorial election according to the Electoral Act?
src_answer: In an election for President or Governor, whether contested or not, the result is ascertained by counting the votes cast for each candidate. The candidate who receives the highest number of votes is declared elected by the appropriate returning officer, subject to sections 133, 134 and 179 of the Constitution [act-s66-0].

question: Kí ni ó gbọ́dọ̀ ṣẹlẹ̀ kí a tó lè fi olùdìbò kan jẹ́ olúborí nínú ìdìbò tí a ń ṣeré fún àwọn iṣẹ́ míìrán?
answer: Fún ìdìbò tí a ń ṣeré fún àwọn iṣẹ́ míìrán tí kì í ṣe Ààrẹ tàbí Gómìnà, àwọn ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ kíkà fún gbogbo àwọn olùdìbò, èsì sì gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ alágbára. Olùdìbò tí ó gba ìdìbò púpọ̀ jù lọ ni yóò jẹ́ olúborí, gẹ́gẹ́ bí àwọn ìwé-òfin kan náà ṣe sọ [act-s66-0].
src_question: What must happen before a candidate can be declared elected in a contested election for other offices?
src_answer: For any contested election to an elective office other than President or Governor, the votes must be counted for each candidate and the result ascertained. The candidate with the highest number of votes is then declared elected by the appropriate returning officer, subject to the same constitutional provisions [act-s66-0].

question: Kí ni Ìjọba Ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe nípa àwọn ìtọ́sọ́nà ìdìbò?
answer: Ìjọba Ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ fi àwọn ìtọ́sọ́nà ìdìbò sílẹ̀ àti kí wọ́n ṣe ìtẹ̀jáde wọn nínú Ìwé-ìròyìn Ìjọba. Àwọn ìtọ́sọ́nà yìí gbọ́dọ̀ ní àwọn ìtọ́sọ́nà fún ìkíkà ìdìbò lọ́nà ìgbà-ìgbà, láti ìlú ìdìbò àti láti ìlú ìdìbò tí ó kẹ́yìn sí ìlú ìdìbò tí ó jẹ́ ti ìjọba ìjọba tàbí ìjọba ìjọba [act-s70-0].
src_question: What is the Commission required to do regarding election guidelines?
src_answer: The Commission shall issue and publish guidelines for the elections in the Federal Government Gazette. These guidelines must include provisions for the step‑by‑step recording of the poll in the electoral forms, beginning at the polling unit and continuing to the last collation centre for the ward or constituency where the result is declared [act-s70-0].

question: Nibo ni ìtẹ̀jáde ìdìbò yìí bẹ̀rẹ̀ àti pé ó parí gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìlànà?
answer: Ìtẹ̀jáde ìdìbò yìí bẹ̀rẹ̀ ní ìlú ìdìbò (polling unit) àti pé ó tẹ̀ síwájú láti ọ̀nà kan sí ọ̀nà mìíràn títí dé ibi ìkópa ìdájọ́ (collation centre) tí ó wà ní ìlú ìdìbò náà. Ìlànà náà ń fún wa láyè láti ṣe ìtẹ̀jáde yìí títí dé ibi tí a ó fi sọ ìdájọ́ náà jáde. [act-s70-0]
src_question: Where does the step‑by‑step recording of the poll start and end according to the guidelines?
src_answer: The recording starts at the polling unit and proceeds through each level until it reaches the last collation centre for the ward or constituency where the result is declared. The guidelines require this process to be followed so that the election result can be declared at the appropriate centre [act-s70-0].

question: Kí ni ìjọba ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe pẹ̀lú ìwé ìdájọ́ ní ìlú ìdìbò gẹ́gẹ́ bí Ìwé Ìṣàkóso Ìdìbò?
answer: Gẹ́gẹ́ bí Ìwé Ìṣàkóso Ìdìbò, ìjọba ìdìbò gbọ́dọ̀ fi àmì ìdájọ́ (stamp), kí wọ́n sì fi àmì ìdájọ́ (sign) àti àmì ìdájọ́ (countersign) sí ìwé ìdájọ́ náà ní ìlú ìdìbò. Àwọn àkọ́kọ́ ìwé ìdájọ́ gbọ́dọ̀ fún àwọn ọlọ́pàá àti àwọn olùṣàkóso ìdìbò ní ìlú ìdìbò ní ìdílé [act-s71-0].
src_question: What must a presiding officer do with the result form at the ward level according to the Electoral Act?
src_answer: According to the Electoral Act, a presiding officer must stamp, sign and countersign the result form at the ward level. Copies must be given to police officers and polling agents where available [act-s71-0].

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ fún olùṣàkóso ìdìbò tí kò fi àmì ìdájọ́ sí ìwé ìdájọ́ láìsí ìdí tó wà?
answer: Olùṣàkóso ìdìbò tí kò fi àmì ìdájọ́ sí ìwé ìdájọ́ láìsí ìdí tó wà ń ṣe ìṣèlú. Lórí ìdájọ́, wọ́n máa ń fún wọn ní ìdájọ́ ìdájọ́ tí ó tó ọ̀dún mẹ́ta láìsí ìdájọ́ fún wọn [act-s71-0].
src_question: What is the penalty for a presiding officer who fails to stamp and sign a ballot paper result sheet without a lawful reason?
src_answer: Such an officer commits an offence. On conviction, they face a minimum of three years imprisonment without an option of fine [act-s71-0].

question: Kí ni ìdínkù owó tí a gbọ́dọ̀ fún olúborí ìdìbò ààrẹ lábẹ́ Òfin Ìdìbò, 2026?
answer: Lábẹ́ Òfin Ìdìbò, 2026, ìdínkù owó tí a gbọ́dọ̀ fún olúborí ìdìbò ààrẹ ni N10,000,000,000 [act-s92-0].
src_question: What is the maximum election expense allowed for a presidential candidate under the Electoral Act, 2026?
src_answer: Under the Electoral Act, 2026, the maximum election expenses for a presidential candidate are set by law. The limit is N10,000,000,000 [act-s92-0].

question: Kí ni ìdínkù owó tí ẹni kan lè fún olúborí ìdìbò gẹ́gẹ́ bí Òfin Ìdìbò, 2026 ṣe sọ?
answer: Òfin Ìdìbò, 2026, ń ṣètò ìdínkù owó fún àwọn olúborí ìdìbò. Ẹni kan lè fún olúborí ìdìbò ní owó tí kò tó N500,000,000 [act-s92-0].
src_question: What is the maximum amount an individual may donate to a candidate according to the Electoral Act, 2026?
src_answer: The Electoral Act, 2026 places a limit on donations to candidates. An individual may donate no more than N500,000,000 [act-s92-0].

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ tí olùṣirò owó yóò rí bí ó bá ṣe àtúnṣe ìwé tí ó jẹ́ mọ́ ìnáwó ìdìbò olúborí?
answer: Bí olùṣirò owó bá ṣe àtúnṣe ìwé tí ó jẹ́ mọ́ ìnáwó ìdìbò olúborí, òfin ń sọ pé ó jẹ́ ẹ̀ṣẹ́. Ìdájọ́ ni láti san owó tí ó tó N5,000,000 tàbí ọdún mẹ́ta ní ẹ̀wọ̀n, tàbí méjèèjì [act-s92-1].
src_question: What penalty does an accountant face if they falsify a document related to a candidate's election expenditure?
src_answer: If an accountant falsifies a document about a candidate's election spending, the law treats it as an offence. The penalty is a fine of at least N5,000,000 or three years imprisonment, or both [act-s92-1].

question: Ṣé olùṣọ́wọ́n lè jẹ́ ìdájọ́ fún ìrànlọ́wọ́ olùdásílẹ̀ láti ṣe àtúnṣe ìwé nípa ìfowópamọ́ ìdìbò?
answer: Olùṣọ́wọ́n tí ó bá ràn olùdásílẹ̀ lọ́wọ́ láti ṣe àtúnṣe ìwé nípa ìfowópamọ́ ìdìbò ń ṣe ẹ̀ṣẹ̀. Ìdájọ́ kan náà ni yóò wà fún un: ìdájọ́ tí kò ní kéré ju N5,000,000 tàbí ọdún mẹ́ta ìgbàjẹ́, tàbí méjèèjì [act-s92-1].
src_question: Can an accountant be punished for helping a candidate forge a document about election donations?
src_answer: An accountant who helps a candidate forge a document about election donations is also committing an offence. The same penalty applies: a fine of not less than N5,000,000 or three years imprisonment, or both [act-s92-1].

question: Kí ni Ìwé Ìdìbò ṣe àlàyé nípa "ìná ìdìbò" fún ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú?
answer: Ìwé Ìdìbò ṣe àlàyé ìná ìdìbò fún ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú ní ọ̀nà tí ó ṣeé ṣe. Wọ́n ni ìná tí a ń lo láti ọjọ́ ìkìlọ̀ títí dé ọjọ́ ìdìbò fún ìdìbò náà [act-s93-0].
src_question: What does the Electoral Act define as "election expenses" for a political party?
src_answer: The Electoral Act defines election expenses for a political party in clear terms. They are the expenses incurred from the notice date up to and including polling day for that election [act-s93-0].

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ tí ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú lè ní bí ó bá kò ṣe ìfihàn ìwé ìná ìdìbò tí a ti ṣàkóso lórí ìgbà?
answer: Ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú tí kò ṣe ìfihàn ìwé ìná ìdìbò tí a ti ṣàkóso lórí ìgbà lè ní ìdájọ́ owó. Ẹgbẹ́ náà lè ní ìdájọ́ tí ó tó N10,000,000, àti pé ilé-ẹjọ́ lè fi N1,000,000 sí i fún ọjọ́ kọ̀ọ̀kan lẹ́yìn ọjọ́ tí ó yẹ títí ìwé náà yóò fi ṣe ìfihàn [act-s93-0].
src_question: What penalty may a political party face if it fails to submit its audited election expenses return on time?
src_answer: A political party that does not submit its audited election expenses return on time faces financial penalties. The party may be fined up to N10,000,000 and the court may add up to N1,000,000 per day for each day after the due date until the return is submitted [act-s93-0].

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ tí ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú ń kojú bí wọ́n bá náà lọ́nà tí ó lé ewu ìnáwó ìdìbò lọ?
answer: Ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú náà ń ṣe ẹ̀ṣẹ̀, tí wọ́n sì ní láti san owó ìdájọ́ tó tó N10,000,000 gẹ́gẹ́ bí ìdájọ́ tó pọ̀ jù. Lẹ́yìn náà, Ẹ̀ka Ìjọba ń gba owó tí ó lé ewu ìnáwó lọ́wọ́ wọn. [act-s93-1]
src_question: What penalty does a political party face if it spends more than the allowed election expenses?
src_answer: The party commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a maximum fine of N10,000,000. In addition, the Commission forfeits the amount by which the expenses exceed the limit [act-s93-1].

question: Níbo ni àwọn èèyàn lè rí ìdájọ́ tí a ti ṣàkóso fún àwọn ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú, àti àwọn àlàyé wo ni wọ́n ní?
answer: Ẹ̀ka Ìjọba ń ṣe ìdájọ́ tí a ti ṣàkóso fún àwọn ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú wúlò fún àwọn èèyàn láti rí ní ilé ìjọba wọn àti àwọn ilé ìjọba ìpínlẹ̀ nígbà tí wọ́n bá ń ṣiṣẹ́. Ìdájọ́ náà ń ṣàkóso orúkọ, adirẹsi, iṣẹ́, àti iye owó tí wọ́n fi ṣe ìrànlọ́wọ́. [act-s93-1]
src_question: Where can the public view the audited returns of political parties and what details are included?
src_answer: The Commission makes the audited returns available for public inspection at its headquarters and state offices during regular business hours. The returns list each contributor’s name, address, occupation, and the amount contributed [act-s93-1].

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ tí ó kéré jù fún ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú tí ó gba ìrànlọ́wọ́ tí ó lé ewu ìnáwó lọ?
answer: Ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú tí ó bá ṣe àìsàn ìrànlọ́wọ́ tí ó lé ewu ìnáwó lọ ní láti san owó ìdájọ́ tí kò ní kéré ju N5,000,000 lọ. Owó tí ó lé ewu ìnáwó náà gbọ́dọ̀ tún wá sí Ẹ̀ka Ìjọba. [act-s94-0]
src_question: What is the minimum fine for a party that accepts a contribution exceeding the prescribed limit?
src_answer: A party that breaches the contribution limit is liable to a fine of not less than N5,000,000. The excess amount must also be forfeited to the Commission [act-s94-0].

question: Nígbà wo ló gbọ́dọ̀ fi ìròyìn ìdúnàdúrà wọn sílẹ̀ sí àjọ INEC?
answer: Ẹgbẹ́ tí ó ń gbé ààrẹ kan kalẹ̀ gbọ́dọ̀ fi ìròyìn ìdúnàdúrà tí àwọn ènìyàn àti àwọn ilé-iṣẹ́ ṣe sílẹ̀ sí àjọ INEC. Ìròyìn yìí gbọ́dọ̀ wá láàárín oṣù mẹ́ta lẹ́yìn ìfihàn èsì ìdìbò [act-s94-0].
src_question: When must a party sponsoring a candidate submit its contribution report to the Commission?
src_answer: The party sponsoring a candidate must file a report of contributions made by individuals and entities to the Commission. This report is due within three months after the announcement of the election results [act-s94-0].

question: Ta ni ń fún àwọn ìdúnàdúrà àti ìrìn àjò ìṣèlú ní ààbò, àti àwọn ẹ̀ka wo ni lè ràn wọn lọ́wọ́?
answer: Alákòóso ọlọ́pàá ní ìpínlẹ̀ kọ̀ọ̀kan àti Ìlú Àpapọ̀ ni ó ń fún wọn ní ààbò tó yẹ. Ọlọ́pàá lè ní ìrànlọ́wọ́ láti ọ̀dọ̀ Ẹgbẹ́ Ìdájọ́ àti Ìdáàbòbò Nàìjíríà àti àwọn ẹ̀ka ààbò ìjọba àpapọ̀ [act-s95-0].
src_question: Who provides security for political rallies and processions and which agencies may assist?
src_answer: The Commissioner of Police in each State and the Federal Capital Territory is responsible for providing adequate security. The Police may be supported by the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps and any other federal security agency [act-s95-0].

question: Kí ni ipa tí ó wà ní ìdínkù ti Ìjọba Ọlọ́pàá Nàìjíríà àti àwọn ẹ̀ka ààbò mìíràn nígbà ìdúnàdúrà ìṣèlú?
answer: Ipa wọn ni láti fún wọn ní ààbò tó yẹ fún ìṣàkóso ìdúnàdúrà àti ìrìn àjò ní ọ̀nà tí ó tọ́ àti láìsí ìjà. Wọ́n lè ṣe iṣẹ́ lábẹ́ ìṣẹ́ òfin nígbà tí wọ́n bá wà níbi ìdúnàdúrà, ṣùgbọ́n wọn ò lè ṣe àwọn iṣẹ́ mìíràn [act-s95-0].
src_question: What is the limited role of the Nigerian Police Force and other security agencies during political rallies?
src_answer: Their role is limited to providing adequate security for the proper and peaceful conduct of rallies and processions. They may act under lawful duty when posted to the event, but cannot perform other functions [act-s95-0].

question: Kí ni èdè tí a kò gbà láti lò nínú ìtànkálẹ̀ ìṣèlú?
answer: Ìtànkálẹ̀ ìṣèlú kò gbọ́dọ̀ lo èdè tí ó lè fa ìbàjẹ́ sí ìmọ̀lára ẹ̀sìn, ẹ̀yà, ìbílẹ̀, tàbí ẹ̀yà ìjọba. Wọ́n tún kò gbọ́dọ̀ lo èdè tí ó jẹ́ ìbàjẹ́, tí ó jẹ́ ìbàjẹ́, tí ó jẹ́ ìṣàlàyé, tàbí tí ó jẹ́ èdè tí ó ṣe láti fa ìdájọ́ ìjà [act-s96-0].
src_question: What kind of language is prohibited in political campaigns?
src_answer: Political campaigns shall not use abusive language likely to injure religious, ethnic, tribal or sectional feelings. They also shall not employ abusive, intemperate, slanderous or base language designed to provoke violent reaction [act-s96-0].

question: Kí ni àwọn ibi tí a kò gbà láti lò fún ìtànkálẹ̀ ìṣèlú, ìrìn-àjò, tàbí ìrìn-àjò?
answer: Àwọn ibi tí a ti yàn fún ìjọsìn, àwọn ẹ̀ka ọlọ́pàá, àti àwọn ilé ìjọba kò gbọ́dọ̀ lò fún ìtànkálẹ̀ ìṣèlú, ìrìn-àjò, tàbí ìrìn-àjò. Wọ́n tún kò gbọ́dọ̀ lò láti gbé ìtànkálẹ̀, láti gbé ìtànkálẹ̀, tàbí láti kọ̀ àwọn ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú, àwọn olùdájọ́, tàbí àwọn ètò wọn [act-s96-0].
src_question: Which locations are not allowed to be used for political campaigns, rallies, or processions?
src_answer: Places designated for religious worship, police stations, and public offices shall not be used for political campaigns, rallies, or processions. They also shall not be used to promote, propagate or attack political parties, candidates, or their programmes [act-s96-0].

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ tí olùdájọ́ ń kojú fún ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ Ìwé-ìṣèlú 96(5)?
answer: Ìwé-ìṣèlú 96(7) sọ pé olùdájọ́ tí ó bá ṣe àìgbọ́ràn sí èyíkéyìí nínú àwọn ìwé-ìṣèlú yìí ni ó ní láti san owó tí ó tó N5,000,000 tàbí láti wà ní ìdájọ́ fún ọdún 12. Nítorí náà, ìdájọ́ fún olùdájọ́ yìí ni owó tí ó tó N5,000,000 tàbí ọdún 12 ìdájọ́ [act-s96-1].
src_question: What penalty does a candidate face for breaking Section 96(5) of the Electoral Act?
src_answer: Section 96(7) of the Electoral Act provides that a candidate who contravenes any provision of this section is liable to a maximum fine of N5,000,000 or imprisonment for a term of 12 months. Consequently, the penalty for such a candidate is a fine up to N5,000,000 or 12 months of imprisonment [act-s96-1].

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ fún ẹnikẹ́ni tó ń ṣèrànwọ́ fún ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú láti ṣẹ́ àṣẹ 96(5)?
answer: Àṣẹ 96(8) sọ pé ẹnikẹ́ni tó ń ṣèrànwọ́ tàbí ń gbìyànjú fún ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú láti ṣẹ́ àṣẹ 96(5) ń ṣe ẹ̀ṣẹ̀, tí ìdájọ́ rẹ̀ ni owó ìdájọ́ tí ó tó N2,000,000, tàbí ìgbà ìdájọ́ tí ó tó ọdún mẹ́ta, tàbí méjèèjì. Nítorí náà, ìdájọ́ fún ẹnikẹ́ni bẹ́ẹ̀ ni owó ìdájọ́ tí ó tó N2,000,000, ọdún mẹ́ta nínú ìdájọ́, tàbí méjèèjì [act-s96-1].
src_question: What is the punishment for someone who helps a political party violate Section 96(5)?
src_answer: Section 96(8) states that any person who aids or abets a political party in contravening subsection (5) commits an offence and is liable to a fine of N2,000,000 or imprisonment for three years, or both. Thus, the punishment for such a person is a fine of N2,000,000, three years in prison, or both [act-s96-1].

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ tí olúborí gba fún ìdàjọ́ olùdìbò pẹ̀lú agbára nígbà ìdìbò?
answer: Ìwé-òfin ìdìbò sọ pé olúborí tí ó bá ṣe ìdàjọ́ olùdìbò pẹ̀lú agbára nígbà ìdìbò ni yóò gba ìdájọ́ tí ó tó N5,000,000 tàbí ìgbà 12 oṣù. Nítorí náà, ìdájọ́ fún olúborí tí ó ṣe ìdàjọ́ bẹ́ẹ̀ ni ìdájọ́ tí ó tó N5,000,000 tàbí ìgbà 12 oṣù [act-s97-0].
src_question: What penalty does a candidate receive for threatening a voter with force during a campaign?
src_answer: Section 97(2)(a) of the Electoral Act says that a candidate who threatens a person with force or violence during a campaign is liable to a maximum fine of N5,000,000 or imprisonment for 12 months. Therefore, the penalty for a candidate who makes such threats is a fine up to N5,000,000 or 12 months of imprisonment [act-s97-0].

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ tí ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú ń fọwọ́ sílẹ̀ fún àwọn olùdìbò?
answer: Ìpínlẹ̀ 97(2)(b) sọ pé ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú tí ó bá ń fọwọ́ sílẹ̀ fún àwọn olùdìbò ni yóò ní ìdájọ́ tí ó tó N10,000,000 fún ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ àkọ́kọ́ àti N2,000,000 fún èyíkéyìí ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí ó bá wáyé lẹ́yìn náà. Nítorí náà, ìdájọ́ fún ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú tí ó bá ń fọwọ́ sílẹ̀ fún àwọn olùdìbò ni N10,000,000 ní ìbẹ̀rẹ̀ àti N2,000,000 fún àwọn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí ó bá wáyé lẹ́yìn náà [act-s97-0].
src_question: What fine does a political party face for threatening voters?
src_answer: Section 97(2)(b) provides that a political party that threatens voters is liable to a fine of N10,000,000 for the first offence and N2,000,000 for any subsequent offence. Hence, the fine for a party that threatens voters is N10,000,000 initially and N2,000,000 for later offences [act-s97-0].

question: Níbo ni àkókò ìgbésẹ̀ ìṣèlú tó wà ní ìlànà ìdìbò ń bẹ̀rẹ̀ àti tó ń parí?
answer: Ìpín 98(1) nínú Ìlànà Ìdìbò sọ pé àkókò ìgbésẹ̀ ìṣèlú ń bẹ̀rẹ̀ ní ọjọ́ 150 ṣáájú ọjọ́ ìdìbò àti pé ó ń parí ní wákàtí 24 ṣáájú ọjọ́ ìdìbò. Nítorí náà, àkókò ìgbésẹ̀ ìṣèlú ń bẹ̀rẹ̀ ní ọjọ́ 150 ṣáájú ọjọ́ ìdìbò àti pé ó ń parí ní wákàtí 24 ṣáájú ọjọ́ ìdìbò [act-s98-0].
src_question: When does the official campaign period start and end according to the Electoral Act?
src_answer: Section 98(1) of the Electoral Act defines the campaign period as commencing 150 days before polling day and ending 24 hours prior to that day. Accordingly, the official campaign period starts 150 days before polling day and ends 24 hours before polling day [act-s98-0].

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ tí ó wà fún ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú tí ó ṣe ìpolówó ìròyìn lórí ẹ̀rọ ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ ní wákàtí 24 ṣáájú ọjọ́ ìdìbò?
answer: Ìpín 98(2) sọ pé ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú tí a ti forúkọ sílẹ̀ tí ó ṣe ìpolówó lórí ẹ̀rọ ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ ní wákàtí 24 ṣáájú ọjọ́ ìdìbò ń ṣe ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ lábẹ́ Ìlànà yìí. Nítorí náà, ẹgbẹ́ bẹ́ẹ̀ lè ní ìdájọ́ tí ó tó N2,000,000 [act-s98-0].
src_question: What penalty applies to a party that runs a broadcast advertisement in the 24 hours before polling day?
src_answer: Section 98(2) states that a registered political party which advertises on broadcasting facilities in the 24 hours before polling day commits an offence under this Act. As a result, such a party is liable to a maximum fine of N2,000,000 [act-s98-0].

question: Kí ni òfin tí ó ń ṣàkóso pé gbogbo àwọn ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú yóò gba àkókò ìpolówó tó jọra lórí ẹ̀rọ ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ gbangba?
answer: Ìpín 99(4) sọ pé lórí ẹ̀rọ ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ gbangba, àkókò ìpolówó gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ tó jọra fún gbogbo àwọn ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú tàbí àwọn olùdìbò ní àkókò àṣeyọrí, ní àkókò tó jọra lọ́jọ́ kọọkan, tí ó bá wà ní ìdíwọ̀ fún ìsanwó owó tó yẹ. Nítorí náà, òfin yìí ń ṣàkóso pé gbogbo àwọn ẹgbẹ́ ìṣèlú yóò gba àkókò ìpolówó tó jọra lórí ẹ̀rọ ìbánisọ̀rọ̀ gbangba [act-s99-0].
src_question: What rule ensures all political parties receive equal airtime on public electronic media?
src_answer: Section 99(4) requires that at any public electronic media, equal airtime shall be allotted to all political parties or candidates during prime times at similar hours each day, subject to payment of appropriate fees. Therefore, the rule ensures all parties receive equal airtime during prime times each day [act-s99-0].

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ tí ilé-ìròyìn gbọ́dọ̀ gba fún kò fún àwọn ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú ní ìdájọ́ tó dọ́gba?
answer: Ìpín 99(6)(a) sọ pé ilé-ìròyìn gbọ́dọ̀ fún àwọn ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú ní ìdájọ́ tó dọ́gba. Tí kò bá ṣe bẹ́ẹ̀, ó ní láti san ìdájọ́ tí ó tó N2,000,000 ní ìgbà àkọ́kọ́, àti N5,000,000 fún àwọn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí ó tẹ̀ lé e. Nítorí náà, ìdájọ́ fún ilé-ìròyìn tí kò fún àwọn ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú ní ìdájọ́ tó dọ́gba ni N2,000,000 ní ìgbà àkọ́kọ́ àti N5,000,000 fún àwọn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ tí ó tẹ̀ lé e [act-s99-0].
src_question: What penalty does a public media house face for not giving equal coverage to parties?
src_answer: Section 99(6)(a) provides that a public media house that contravenes the equal coverage rules is liable to a fine of N2,000,000 in the first instance and N5,000,000 for subsequent convictions. Consequently, the penalty for a public media house that fails to give equal coverage is a fine of N2,000,000 initially and N5,000,000 for later offences [act-s99-0].

question: Kí ni àwọn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ ìgbàlódè tí a kò gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe lórí ọjọ́ ìdìbò gẹ́gẹ́ bí Ìwé-òfin Ìdìbò, 2026?
answer: Ìwé-òfin Ìdìbò, 2026 kò gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe àwọn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ ìgbàlódè, bíi ìtẹ̀jáde, ìtẹ̀jáde, ìtẹ̀jáde, tàbí ìtẹ̀jáde àwọn ìwé ìròyìn, ìwé ìròyìn, ìwé ìròyìn, tàbí ìtẹ̀jáde àwọn ìwé ìròyìn, láti gbìyànjú tàbí láti kọ́ ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú tàbí olùdìbò lórí ọjọ́ ìdìbò tàbí 24 wákàtí tí ó tẹ̀ lé e [act-s100-0]. Ìdàkọ̀ yìí ṣàkóso sí redio, tẹlísíònù, ìwé ìròyìn, ìwé ìròyìn, ìwé ìròyìn, àti àwọn ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ ìgbàlódè míì.
src_question: What broadcasting activities are prohibited on polling day according to the Electoral Act, 2026?
src_answer: The Electoral Act, 2026 prohibits any person, print or electronic medium from broadcasting, publishing, advertising or circulating material to promote or oppose a political party or candidate on polling day or the 24 hours immediately preceding it [act-s100-0]. The ban covers radio, television, newspapers, magazines, handbills and any other print or electronic media.

question: Kí ni àwọn ìdájọ́ fún ẹni tí ó bá ṣe ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ ìgbàlódè lórí ọjọ́ ìdìbò?
answer: Lábẹ́ Ìwé-òfin, ẹni tí a bá gbà pé ó ṣe ìṣẹ̀lẹ̀ ìgbàlódè lórí ọjọ́ ìdìbò ní láti san ìdájọ́ tí ó tó N3,000,000 sí N5,000,000 [act-s100-0]. Ilé-ẹjọ́ lè tún fi ẹni náà sí ìdájọ́ ìdájọ́ fún oṣù mẹ́fà tàbí láti fi ìdájọ́ àti ìdájọ́ sí i.
src_question: What are the penalties for an individual who violates the broadcast prohibition on polling day?
src_answer: Under the Act, an individual convicted faces a minimum fine of N3,000,000 and a maximum fine of N5,000,000 [act-s100-0]. The court may also impose imprisonment for six months or both fine and imprisonment.

question: Kí ni tó gbọ́dọ̀ ṣẹlẹ̀ ṣáájú kí Ìgbìmọ̀ Ìṣèjọba Agbègbè lè gbìyànjú láti ṣàwárí ẹ̀sùn ìwà ìṣekúṣe tó pọ̀ síi lórí Ààrẹ?
answer: Ìkìlọ̀ nípa ẹ̀sùn náà gbọ́dọ̀ kọ, tí a sì fi àmì sílẹ̀, tí ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ mẹ́ta lára àwọn ọmọ Ìgbìmọ̀ Ìṣèjọba Agbègbè yóò sì fi sílẹ̀, tí wọ́n sì gbọ́dọ̀ fún Ààrẹ àti gbogbo àwọn ọmọ Ìgbìmọ̀ ní àkọ́kọ́ lábẹ́ ọ̀sẹ̀ méje. Ìgbìmọ̀ náà gbọ́dọ̀ sì pinnu lábẹ́ ọ̀sẹ̀ méjìlá bóyá wọ́n yóò gbìyànjú láti ṣàwárí ẹ̀sùn náà nípa ìgbésẹ̀ láìsí ìdájọ́. [act-s114-0]
src_question: What must happen before the Area Legislative Council can vote on investigating an allegation of gross misconduct against the Chairman?
src_answer: A notice of the allegation must be written, signed by at least one‑third of the council members, and presented to the Speaker [act-s114-0]. The Leader must serve a copy on the Chairman and all members within seven days, and the council must then decide within 14 days whether to investigate by motion without debate.

question: Kí ni ìdájọ́ tí a gbọ́dọ̀ ní láti fi ìgbésẹ̀ láti ṣàwárí ẹ̀sùn náà kọjá?
answer: Ìgbésẹ̀ náà gbọ́dọ̀ ní ìdájọ́ ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ mẹ́ta láti ọ̀pọ̀ àwọn ọmọ Ìgbìmọ̀ Ìṣèjọba Agbègbè láti kọjá [act-s114-0]. Nígbà náà ni ìgbésẹ̀ náà yóò jẹ́ pé ó ti kọjá.
src_question: What majority vote is required for the motion to investigate the allegation to be passed?
src_answer: The motion must be supported by the votes of not less than two‑thirds majority of all the members of the Area Legislative Council [act-s114-0]. Only then is the motion declared as having been passed.

question: Ta ni ó ń yàn àjọ láti ṣàwárí ẹ̀sùn náà, àti kí ni àwọn ìwà ìṣòdodo tí àwọn ọmọ àjọ náà gbọ́dọ̀ ní?
answer: Lábẹ́ ọ̀sẹ̀ méje lẹ́yìn ìgbésẹ̀ náà, Ààrẹ ń fún Olúbàdọ́gba ní ìròyìn, tí ó sì ń yàn àjọ mẹ́jọ tí kò ní ìṣòdodo tí kò ní ìdájọ́ [act-s114-1]. Àwọn ọmọ àjọ náà kò gbọ́dọ̀ jẹ́ ọmọ ìjọba, ọmọ iṣẹ́ ìjọba, ọmọ Ìgbìmọ̀ Ìṣèjọba, tàbí ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ òṣèlú.
src_question: Who appoints the panel to investigate the allegation and what qualifications must the panel members have?
src_answer: Within seven days of the motion, the Leader informs the Chief Judge who appoints a panel of seven persons of unquestionable integrity [act-s114-1]. The panel members must not be members of any public or civil service, a legislative house, or a political party.

question: Báwo ló ṣe ń lọ fún àkókò tí àjọ ìṣèlú gbọ́dọ̀ fi gbé ìwádìí wọn kalẹ̀, àti àwọn ẹ̀tọ́ tí ẹni tí a ń ṣàwárí ní ní nígbà tí wọ́n ń ṣàwárí?
answer: Àjọ ìṣèlú gbọ́dọ̀ fi ìwádìí wọn kalẹ̀ sí Àjọ Ìṣèlú Agbègbè láàárín oṣù mẹ́ta lẹ́yìn tí wọ́n ti yàn wọn [act-s114-1]. Ẹni tí ó wà nípò lè dá ara rẹ̀ dúró ní ara rẹ̀ tàbí kó ní ìrànlọ́wọ́ láti ọ̀dọ̀ olùkọ́ni òfin tí ó yàn fúnra rẹ̀.
src_question: How long does the panel have to submit its findings and what rights does the accused have during the investigation?
src_answer: The panel must report its findings to the Area Legislative Council within three months of its appointment [act-s114-1]. The holder of the office may defend himself in person or be represented by a legal practitioner of his or her own choice.

question: Ní àwọn ìpò wo ni Ààrẹ tàbí Olùdájọ́ Agbègbè lè yọ kúrò nípò?
answer: Ààrẹ tàbí Olùdájọ́ Agbègbè lè yọ kúrò nípò bí àwọn èèyàn méjì nínú mẹ́ta tí ó wà nínú Ìgbìmọ̀ Ìṣàkóso bá sọ pé ẹni náà kò lè ṣe iṣẹ́ rẹ̀, àti pé ìwé ìdánilójú ìṣègùn tí ó jẹ́rìí sí èyí ni àjọ ìṣègùn yóò fi hàn [act-s115-0]. Àjọ ìṣègùn náà ní àwọn oníṣègùn mẹ́fà ní orílẹ̀-èdè Nàìjíríà, tí ẹni kan nínú wọn ni oníṣègùn ara ẹni tí ó wà nípò, àti àwọn mẹ́rin mìíràn tí Ààrẹ yóò fi hàn pé wọ́n ní ìmọ̀ tó pọ̀.
src_question: Under what conditions can the Chairman or Vice‑Chairman of an Area Council be removed from office?
src_answer: The Chairman or Vice‑Chairman ceases to hold office if a two‑thirds majority of all members of the Executive Council declares the holder incapable of performing the functions, and this declaration is verified by a medical panel report [act-s115-0]. The medical panel consists of five medical practitioners in Nigeria, including the personal physician of the office holder, and four other practitioners deemed highly qualified by the Speaker.

question: Kí ni àwọn èèyàn tí ó wà nínú àjọ ìṣègùn tí ó ń ṣàwárí pé ẹni kan kò lè ṣe iṣẹ́ rẹ̀?
answer: Àjọ ìṣègùn náà ni Ààrẹ yóò yàn, ó sì gbọ́dọ̀ ní àwọn oníṣègùn mẹ́fà, tí ẹni kan nínú wọn ni oníṣègùn ara ẹni tí ó wà nípò, àti àwọn mẹ́rin mìíràn tí Ààrẹ yóò fi hàn pé wọ́n ní ìmọ̀ tó pọ̀ [act-s115-0]. Lẹ́yìn náà, ìwé ìdánilójú àjọ ìṣègùn yóò wáyé nínú Ìwé Ìròyìn Ìjọba láti mú kí ẹni náà yọ kúrò nípò.
src_question: What is the composition of the medical panel that verifies the Chairman's incapacity?
src_answer: The medical panel is appointed by the Speaker and must consist of five medical practitioners in Nigeria, one of whom is the personal physician of the holder of the office, and four other medical practitioners who have attained a high level of qualification in the opinion of the Speaker [act-s115-0]. The panel’s report is then published in the Official Gazette to effect the removal.

question: Kí ni tó má ṣẹlẹ sí ipò Olùdarí Àgbà Àgbègbè bí Olùdarí Àgbà Àgbègbè bá kú tàbí kó ìdájọ́ rẹ̀?
answer: Ìpín 116(1) sọ pé Olùdájọ́ Àgbà Àgbègbè yóò gbé ipò Olùdarí Àgbà Àgbègbè bí ipò náà bá ṣubú nítorí ikú, ìdájọ́, àìsàn tàbí ìyọkúrò gẹ́gẹ́ bí Ìpín 112 tàbí 113 ti Òfin yìí. Ìpín 116(2) ṣàfikún pé bí Olùdájọ́ Àgbà Àgbègbè náà bá ṣubú, Olùdásílẹ̀ Àgbègbè Àgbègbè yóò gbé ipò Olùdarí Àgbà Àgbègbè fún àkókò tí kò kéré ju oṣù mẹ́ta lọ, nígbà tí ìdìbò fún Olùdarí Àgbà Àgbègbè tuntun yóò wáyé. [act-s116-0]
src_question: What happens to the position of Chairman of an Area Council if the Chairman dies or resigns?
src_answer: Section 116(1) states that the Vice-Chairman of an Area Council shall hold the office of the Chairman if the office becomes vacant by reason of death, resignation, permanent incapacity or removal in accordance with section 112 or 113 of this Act. Section 116(2) adds that if the Vice-Chairman is also vacant, the Speaker of the Area Legislative Council shall hold office of the Chairman for not less than three months, during which an election of a new Chairman shall be held. [act-s116-0]

question: Bí Alága Ìgbìmọ̀ Agbè kan bá kúrò nípò fún èyíkéyìí ìdí, bawo ni a ṣe ń yan Alága Ìgbìmọ̀ Agbè tuntun?
answer: Ìsàlẹ̀ 116(3) sọ pé Alága ni yóò gbìyànjú Alága Ìgbìmọ̀ Agbè tuntun. Lẹ́yìn náà, Alága yóò yan ẹni tí ó gbìyànjú pẹ̀lú ìfọwọ́sí ẹ̀ka ìṣèjọba Ìgbìmọ̀ Agbè. [act-s116-0]
src_question: If the Vice-Chairman of an Area Council leaves office for any reason, how is a new Vice-Chairman appointed?
src_answer: Section 116(3) states that the Chairman shall nominate a new Vice-Chairman. The Chairman then appoints the nominee with the approval of the legislative arm of the Area Council. [act-s116-0]

question: Kí ni àkókò tí a gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe ìgbéyàwó láti mú kí ọmọ ẹgbẹ́ Ìgbìmọ̀ Ìlú kan padà?
answer: Ìpínlẹ̀ 117(b) sọ pé ìgbéyàwó gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe láàárín ọjọ́ 90 lẹ́yìn tí ìwé ìbéèrè bá dé lọ́wọ́ Kọ́míṣọ̀nà. Ìgbéyàwó gbọ́dọ̀ gba àṣẹ láti ọ̀dọ̀ ọ̀pọ̀lọpọ̀ àwọn ènìyàn tí wọ́n wà nínú ìlú náà. [act-s117-0]
src_question: What is the time limit for holding a referendum to recall an Area Council member?
src_answer: Section 117(b) mandates that the referendum must be conducted within 90 days of the date the petition is received by the Commission. The referendum must be approved by a simple majority of the votes of the persons registered to vote in that member's constituency. [act-s117-0]

question: Kí ni àwọn ìṣe tí a ka sí ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ lábẹ́ Ìpínlẹ̀ 118(a) àti (b) nínú Òfin Ìdìbò?
answer: Ìpínlẹ̀ 118(a) sọ pé ó jẹ́ ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ láti pa, pa àwọn, ṣe àìsàn, yọ, tàbí yí padà àwọn ìtọ́sọ́nà tàbí àwọn ìwé tí a nílò fún ìṣàkóso ìwé ìdìbò. Ìpínlẹ̀ 118(b) sọ pé ó jẹ́ ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ láti wá síbẹ̀ láti jẹ́ tàbí ṣe àwọn ìṣe tí ó mú kí ẹnì kan wà nínú ìwé àwọn ènìyàn tí wọ́n wà nínú ìdìbò fún ìlú tí ẹnì náà kò ní ìdájọ́ láti wà nínú rẹ̀, tàbí láti mú kí ẹnì kan wà nínú ìwé àwọn ènìyàn tí wọ́n wà nínú ìdìbò ní àwọn ìgbà méjì. [act-s118-0]
src_question: Which actions are considered offences under Section 118(a) and (b) of the Electoral Act?
src_answer: Section 118(a) makes it an offence to without authority destroy, mutilate, deface, remove or alter any notice or document required for the purpose of registration under this Act. Section 118(b) makes it an offence to present oneself to be or do any act whereby one is included in the register of voters for a constituency in which one is not entitled to be registered or to cause oneself to be registered in more than one registration or revision centre. [act-s118-0]

question: Kí ni àwọn ìṣe tí a kò gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe lábẹ́ Ìpínlẹ̀ 118(c) àti (d) nínú Òfin Ìdìbò?
answer: Ìpínlẹ̀ 118(c) kò gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe àwọn ìtọ́sọ́nà tàbí ìròyìn tí a mọ̀ pé ó jẹ́ òtítọ́ tàbí tí a kò gbà gbọ́ pẹ̀lú ìfẹ́ láti dènà àwọn ènìyàn tí wọ́n ní ìdájọ́ láti wà nínú ìdìbò. Ìpínlẹ̀ 118(d) kò gbọ́dọ̀ ṣe àwọn ìtọ́sọ́nà tàbí ìròyìn tí ó jẹ́ òtítọ́ nínú àwọn ìwé, ìwé ìdìbò, tàbí àwọn ìwé tí a nílò fún ìṣàkóso ìwé ìdìbò. [act-s118-0]
src_question: What actions are prohibited under Section 118(c) and (d) of the Electoral Act?
src_answer: Section 118(c) prohibits publishing any statement or report known to be false or not believed to be true with the intent to prevent qualified persons from registering as voters. Section 118(d) prohibits making any false entry or statement in any record, register or document required for registration purposes. [act-s118-0]

question: Kí ni àwọn ìṣe tó jẹ́ ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ lábẹ́ Ìpín 119(1)?
answer: Ìpín 119(1)(a) ń ṣe ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ láti ṣe àtúnṣe tàbí ṣe àtúnṣe àwọn ìwé ìfẹ̀sẹ̀wọnsẹ̀ tàbí àwọn ìwé ìdájọ́ ìfẹ̀sẹ̀wọnsẹ̀, àti Ìpín 119(1)(b) ń ṣe ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ láti ṣe àtúnṣe tàbí pa àwọn ìwé ìfẹ̀sẹ̀wọnsẹ̀ tàbí àwọn ìwé ìdájọ́ ìfẹ̀sẹ̀wọnsẹ̀ lọ́wọ́. Ìpín 119(1)(c) ń ṣe ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ láti fi àwọn ìwé ìfẹ̀sẹ̀wọnsẹ̀ tàbí àwọn ìwé ìdájọ́ ìfẹ̀sẹ̀wọnsẹ̀ sí ọ̀dọ̀ olùṣàkóso ìdájọ́ tí ó mọ̀ pé wọ́n ti ṣe àtúnṣe, àti Ìpín 119(1)(d) ń ṣe ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ láti fi orúkọ rẹ̀ sí àwọn ìwé ìfẹ̀sẹ̀wọnsẹ̀ gẹ́gẹ́ bí olùdájọ́ ní àwọn ìlú púpọ̀ ní ìdájọ́ kan náà. [act-s119-0]
src_question: What nomination-related actions are offences under Section 119(1)?
src_answer: Section 119(1)(a) makes it an offence to forge any nomination paper or result form, and Section 119(1)(b) makes it an offence to willfully deface or destroy any nomination paper or result form. Section 119(1)(c) makes it an offence to deliver a nomination paper or result form to an electoral officer knowing it to be forged, and Section 119(1)(d) makes it an offence to sign a nomination paper as a candidate in more than one constituency at the same election. [act-s119-0]

question: Kí ni àwọn ìṣe tó jẹ́ ẹ̀ṣẹ̀ lábẹ́ Ìpín 119(1)?
